note: Block A tasks that come from no screen or operation, so the slice cannot derive them. Read by tools/build-service-docs.py. Edit this file, not the task sheet. Added 30 September 2026 from the system-design review (audit/ticvai/steps/SD, findings SD-016, 024, 026, 028, 030-032, 034, 046-049, 051, 057, 059, 063) and the AI functions review (docs/active/ai-functions-review-30-september.md). `pool: backend` goes to the least-loaded backend owner; `assignee` names a person. AI engine tasks carry no points: they are sized in engineer-days in their text and planned by the two AI engineers, whose capacity is separate from the developers' (decided 30 September). Since 1 October a task may carry `block` (for example `B1`): it is recorded here with the ADR that asks for it and is not ticketed in the Block A sheet; build-service-docs.py skips it until that block is planned. A task without `block` is Block A. Since 1 October (the sprint plan) a later-block task names the app-module it lands in with `module` (a business module) and `platform` (P01-P17; none = that module's platform work), and build-service-docs.py plans it with the rest of the package. **The Block A AI chain split across both AI engineers** (Chinmay, 1 October): the baseline layer (estimators, venue profile, starting patterns) and Qdrant tenancy do not call the LLM gateway, so they start on day one beside it; day-one suggestions and the evaluation harness still wait for the gateway (an answer is recorded through its decision point), and the concierge for Qdrant. Kalpita Mejari: gateway, concierge, Help me choose, translations, planner (33 days); the second AI engineer: baseline, Qdrant, suggestions, evaluation (33 days). `appModule: baseline` puts a task in the second AI engine app-module of Block A, so each engineer's module test is of the other's half. **Block A completes its apps** (Chinmay, 3 October 2026, CHG-RONEP-001; docs/active/decisions/answers-3-october-r1-plan.md): an AI engine task's `operations` are served by ticvai-ai and built by that task, not by a back-end task; `blockAOperations` and `blockAScreens` are decided Block A scope no screen binding in this tree derives (each with its reason); `screenNotes` is a sentence a screen's tasks carry; `departures` records why an artefact an earlier released plan built in a ticketed block is no longer built there (tools/check-plan-closure.py fails on one without a reason). **Two drops** (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-007): `blockA1Operations` are needed by A1 itself; `blockAOperations`, `blockAScreens` and the rest of the setup screens are completion work that goes to A1 app by app while A1 still ends by 27 November, else to A2; `navHomes` are the app homes the navigation closure may pull in besides each app's entry (lever A). **`drop: A2`** (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-010): a Block A AI engine task built in Block A2 instead, so the AI engineers' A1 work ends before 24 November with no overtime. **`due`** (an ISO date; the lead, 20 October 2026, CHG-R8INT-032): a task with a named `assignee` that is due on that date, such as the r8 database updates: the schedule places it on that date's working day, whatever its build order, so it lands in that date's sprint; a chore of under a day, it holds no slot on its owner's calendar, re-paces nothing, is in nobody's load and has no module test (tools/sprint_plan.py due_of).

tasks.subject: Request kernel: hostname to tenant routing, per-transaction scope, error model and 429
tasks.detail: In ticvai-backend. Resolve the tenant from the hostname (control-plane routing table, SD-021), open every transaction with the tenant and scope settings the row-level policies read (SD-059), one problem-details error model, and 429 with Retry-After on the hot public operations (SD-043). Done when: two seeded tenants on two hostnames cannot read each other's rows, and a flood test returns 429 instead of 500. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): the routing table is `control.tenant_domain` (hostname, verified, redirect) in the control database, joined to `control.tenant` and `control.cell_tenant` for the tenant's cell and database (ADR-0038: one database per tenant inside its region's cell; ADR-0039: `control` is a database of its own and `control.cell` has no tenant_id, the relation is `control.cell_tenant`). The row-level policies of backend/tenant/920-row-level-security.sql read two session settings, set with SET LOCAL at the start of every transaction from the resolved session: `ticvai.scope_paths` (the comma-separated ltree scope paths the principal may see; unset or empty means no rows) and `ticvai.subject_id` (the guest's own rows), and `ticvai.principal_id` (the signed-in principal, for the rows that are its own: credentials and second factors). Venues stay partitions of the tenant database (ADR-0005), not databases. **The context before and without a session** (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C48, the lead's option A, 20 October 2026; CHG-R8MIG-007; backend/MIGRATIONS.md "The connection context"): (1) a door or anonymous call (login, the guest sign-ins, listSsoProviders, listActiveSessions with step-up) opens its transaction in an explicit system context (the tenant root path) confined to the identity module's own verification statements, then narrows it with SET LOCAL before any other table is touched: `ticvai.scope_paths` to the resolved principal's paths and `ticvai.principal_id` to the principal, or `ticvai.subject_id` to the guest (scope paths empty); a session-less till call narrows to the till's venue path once the supervisor is verified; (2) a guest reads and writes its own `pii.subject` row and the rows keyed to its subject; (3) a serviceAuth cell-internal call has no user: the tenant comes from the cell token's tid claim, `ticvai.scope_paths` is the tenant root, the calling cell is the audited actor, and its idempotency records are claimed under that context.

tasks.subject: Durable idempotency: the Idempotency-Key store and middleware
tasks.detail: Idempotency records in PostgreSQL with Redis as a cache only (SD-024), so a retried payment or sale after a restart returns the first answer. Done when: replaying a createOrder with the same key after a service restart returns the original response and creates nothing.

tasks.subject: Outbox, relay and inbox behind the kernel broker interface, on a local RabbitMQ
tasks.detail: The transactional outbox per tenant database; one relay per region in the workers host, with a lease and a polling loop per tenant database, and an inbox per tenant database for exactly-once handling (ADR-0058); modules enqueue through IOutbox inside their own transaction, the relay publishes through IBrokerPublisher and consumers subscribe through IEventSubscriber (ADR-0058 amendment, 1 October); the relay drains a full batch at once and its batch size is configuration (Relay:BatchSize, 1,000 in the flash-sale environment). The broker per ADR-0057 is the client's choice between RabbitMQ and Kafka: build behind the kernel interface on a local RabbitMQ until they answer, with ordering per aggregate by an ordering key and dead letters drained into platform.dead_letter. A relay-lag dashboard and alert per tenant database (SD-030, SD-031, SD-032). Done when: an event written in a transaction reaches its consumer once, survives a relay restart and a redelivery, a poison message lands in platform.dead_letter, and relay lag shows on the dashboard and alerts when unpublished rows are older than 60 seconds.

tasks.subject: Republish from the outbox by tenant and time range
tasks.detail: The recovery path for a lost broker (ADR-0058 amendment, 1 October; the DR design in ADR-0060 relies on it): republishOutbox, listOutboxRepublishes, getOutboxRepublish and cancelOutboxRepublish in the operations host, carried out by the relay in workers with a keyset cursor over the outbox, published_at left untouched and live batches first; one job per tenant (control.outbox_republish). Done when: after a simulated broker loss, a republish of one tenant's last hour redelivers every event once to each consumer, the inbox drops the duplicates, and a second request for the same tenant while one runs is refused with 409.

tasks.subject: Order paid to tickets issued: the saga proven end to end
tasks.detail: order.paid consumed by the entitlement owner, tickets issued, the ledger posting once from the event, and holds converted with capacity decremented (SD-026, SD-023). Done when: a web purchase in the sandbox ends with a ticket, one ledger posting and sold capacity reduced, and a replayed event changes nothing. **Until the client's payment sandbox credentials arrive (CLIENT-PAY-SANDBOX)**, 'in the sandbox' is met as PLATFORM-PAYMENTS' module test meets it (CHG-FXP-006): the payment confirmation is a signed webhook built from the provider's documented test payloads with a locally generated signing secret (the lead, 20 October 2026, r8 cause FOUNDATION-AI-C18, option A). The same purchase run against the provider's test mode is a Block A closing check once the credentials arrive, not a condition of this task. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), from events/order-paid.yaml and events/entitlement-issued.yaml (adam_search order.paid): the payment transaction (createPayment, or the provider webhook) converts the inventory holds (`catalogue#convertInventoryHold`: the hold becomes sold capacity), posts the cash receipt to ledger.journal_entry and ledger.journal_line, and writes `order.paid` to the outbox in the same transaction; AccessService consumes it (`access#issueOrderEntitlements`, idempotency key orderId + lineId; on failure retry, then dead-letter, which pages) and publishes `entitlement.issued`; the orders consumer of that completes the order. A dead-lettered issuance is replayed, never compensated by an automatic refund. ADR-0055: modules in different deployables talk by event; ADR-0058: one relay per region and an inbox per tenant database, so a replayed event is a no-op.

tasks.subject: Payment adapter and signed webhook against the provider's test mode
tasks.detail: The provider adapter, the inbound signed webhook, the provider reference on payments, 3-D Secure redirect states and the card-terminal flow for the POS (SD-034). Done when: an approved, a declined and a 3-D Secure payment each end in the right order state from the webhook alone, with polling only as the fallback. Acceptance of the declined, unknown and reconcile paths waits on the client's payment sandbox credentials: see the client's answer in the Decisions Register. Until the client's sandbox credentials arrive (CLIENT-PAY-SANDBOX), the three outcomes are proven with signed webhook fixtures built from the provider's documented test payloads and a locally generated signing secret (CHG-FXP-006); the run against the provider's test mode follows when they arrive and is the acceptance of those paths.

Spec (default taken 4 October, CHG-FXP-005; for the lead to confirm): flags live in Azure App Configuration in the cell's region, read by every .NET host through Microsoft.FeatureManagement with a tenant targeting filter; a flag's key is an app-module key of the plan (for example `AM-MARKETING-CRM-P01`) and covers that app-module's screens and the operations they bind (their `apis` in screens/*.yaml). Off for a tenant: the apps leave its screens out of that tenant's navigation, and the kernel answers its operations with the shared 404 problem of contracts/shared/common.yaml, as if absent. tasks.subject: Row-level policies without a per-row subquery on hot tables
tasks.detail: Scope predicates read session settings instead of joining per row (SD-016). Done when: the order and scan-event queries keep their plan with policies on, measured with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) on the seed data before and after (the before is the baseline). Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): the policies are generated in backend/tenant/920-row-level-security.sql by `platform.apply_scope_rls` and its siblings; today each USING clause calls `platform.in_scope(scope_path)`, which unnests `ticvai.scope_paths` for every row. On the hot tables linked here, rewrite the predicate so the planner evaluates the session setting once per statement (an InitPlan over `platform.current_scope_paths()`) instead of per row; the policy names and deny-by-default stay. **No venue partitioning in release 1** (ADR-0044 as amended by ADR-0056, 30 September; r8 walk fix, CHG-R8WFC-008): `orders.sales_order` is not partitioned, and `access.scan_event` is range-partitioned by month on `recorded_at`, so the predicate keeps that time pruning and no `venue_id = ANY(...)` partition pruning is asked for.

tasks.subject: Observability with tenant and venue on every trace, and the first dashboards
tasks.detail: OpenTelemetry attributes for tenant, venue and workstation; dashboards for the sale path and sync; alerts on error rate and latency (SD-048). Done when: a failed POS sale can be found by venue and till within a minute. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), docs/architecture/observability.md: every log, metric and span carries tenant_id, region_id and venue_id (plus cell, correlation and session id on traces, and workstation on POS metrics), set by the kernel from the resolved session and the workstation. The sale path is the operations linked here (createOrder and createPayment in OrderService, validateAccess in AccessService); sync is syncOrders and syncScans. The first alerts are that document's table, with the threshold, window and severity each row gives (proposed defaults, client to confirm; r8, FOUNDATION-AI-C25): error rate (5xx above 1 percent for 5 minutes; 402 and 409 refusals do not count), latency (p95 above the operation's x-ticvai-latency-budget-ms for 10 minutes), outbox backlog per device (above 1,000 rows or the oldest older than 5 minutes), replication lag per cell (above 30 seconds for 5 minutes), Redis-Postgres capacity divergence and the venue edge heartbeat (missing for 2 minutes), on the stack SETUP-OBS sets up. PgBouncer pool saturation is in that table too but is built by OBS-TENANT-POOL, not here (FOUNDATION-AI-C53).

tasks.subject: Migration fan-out across tenant databases, and expand-then-contract changes
tasks.detail: Apply a migration to every tenant database with progress and resume, and the rule that a schema change ships in two steps so old and new code both run (SD-049). Done when: a column rename reaches three seeded tenant databases with no downtime. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), ADR-0039 section 3: the fan-out unit is a tenant database and the canary is a tenant inside a canary cell; one `control.migration_run_tenant` row per tenant per run (status, from_version, to_version, error, timings), with `control.migration_run_cell` as the rollup; `control.migration_plan_cell` names all tenants of a cell or a named set. A failed tenant stops its wave and is resumed from its row; tenants already done stay done.

tasks.subject: Hosts for the deployables on .NET 10: commerce, access, operations and workers, each composing its modules
tasks.detail: In **ticvai-backend**, on .NET 10 LTS (decided 30 September; ADR-0055), in the clean-architecture solution the setup zip creates (`TICVAI.Domain`, `TICVAI.Contracts`, `TICVAI.Application`, `TICVAI.Infrastructure`, `TICVAI.Api`; repos/ticvai-docs/setup/backend-patterns.md 3.2). Four hosts: commerce (Identity, Tenancy, Catalogue, Order, Ledger, Wallet), access (Access), operations (F&B, Retail, Inventory, VenueOps, Marketing, WhiteLabel, Reporting, Platform, CrossRegion) and workers (the outbox relay, every module's event consumers, scheduled jobs). **A module is a folder, not an assembly**: `TICVAI.Application/Features/<Module>/` with its controllers in `TICVAI.Api`, so a host composes its modules by registering those folders' services and controllers (there is no `IModule` and no `Ticvai.Modules.*` project; r8 walk fix, CHG-R8WFC-008). ticvai-ai stays the Python service. Done when: each host starts locally with its modules registered and a health endpoint, CI builds one image per host, and moving a module to another host is a change of one registration.
tasks.linksNothingBecause: the hosts and their solution layout, infrastructure only; its text names them

tasks.subject: Architecture tests for 17 modules: no module references another, and no module's SQL names another's schema
tasks.detail: Extend `TICVAI.ArchitectureTests` (repos/ticvai-docs/setup/backend-patterns.md 3.2, which already enforces the layer rules: Domain references nothing, Application only Domain and Contracts) to the 17 modules of ADR-0055. A module is a folder, `TICVAI.Application/Features/<Module>/`, not a `Ticvai.Modules.*` assembly (r8 walk fix, CHG-R8WFC-008), so the tests work on namespaces: no type in `Features.<A>` references a type in `Features.<B>` (they share only `TICVAI.Domain` and `TICVAI.Contracts`), and a module's SQL names no other module's schema except through a published read view. Done when: a deliberate cross-module reference and a raw cross-schema query each fail the build in CI.
tasks.linksNothingBecause: architecture tests over the code, not a package artefact; its text names the test file

tasks.subject: Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage
tasks.detail: A deriver reads handoff/api-data-lineage.json and generates, per owning module, the views other modules may read (894 cross-schema reads on 30 September; ADR-0055), applied by the migrations. Done when: every cross-schema read in the Block A slice goes through a published view, the views regenerate with one command, each exposing exactly the union of its readers' `readColumns` (every pii view a column list, never all columns), and a raw cross-schema read is reported by the lineage check. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), ADR-0055 rule 2: another module reads a schema only through views its owner publishes (or the owner's in-process query interface), never raw tables; the owner is the schema's module in handoff/service-decomposition.json. Default for the shape: one view per (reader module, owned table) pair the lineage actually reads, in the owner's schema, named `<table>_for_<reader module>`, exposing only the columns the reader's operations read, with SELECT granted to the reader's deployable role (DB-ROLES). The columns are generated, not chosen (14 October, ADAM CR-004, CHG-LIN-001): each lineage entry carries `readColumns` ({table: [columns]}, derived by tools/derive-read-columns.py from the response schemas, the parameters, the join keys and docs/active/read-columns-override.yaml), and a view's columns are the union of `readColumns[table]` over the reader module's operations that read the table. A read with no list keeps every column, except over pii.*: every cross-module read of a pii table has a list (check-read-columns fails one without), so a pii view is always narrow and is never built over all columns. Reads routed `analytical` go to the reporting replica, never the primary (ADR-0016).
tasks.linksNothingBecause: the views are generated from handoff/api-data-lineage.json; the rules and the naming are in its text

tasks.subject: One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only
tasks.detail: In ticvai-backend, created by the baseline migration (MIG-BASELINE), one PostgreSQL login role per deployable of ADR-0055: commerce, access, operations, workers and ticvai_ai, each reading its password or token from the cell's Key Vault. Each role gets USAGE and SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on the schemas its modules own (the schema owners in handoff/service-decomposition.json; workers runs every module's consumers, the outbox relay and the scheduled jobs, so it gets the schemas those touch), SELECT on the published read views of DB-READ-VIEWS, and nothing else: no CREATE, no ownership, no BYPASSRLS, so FORCE row-level security applies to every host. ticvai_ai writes only the ai schema (and ai.inbox; ADR-0058) and is read-only on the transactional schemas (ADR-0020). The tables are owned by a separate migration role that only SqlMigrationRunner uses. Done when: each host connects with its own role from Key Vault; an INSERT from the ticvai_ai role into a transactional table, and from the commerce role into an operations schema (fnb), are each refused by PostgreSQL; no host role has BYPASSRLS or owns a table (a query on pg_roles and pg_tables in CI shows it); and a host role with no scope set on its session reads no rows from a table under FORCE row-level security. The schemas each role owns (handoff/service-decomposition.json under ADR-0055's five deployables, 4 October, CHG-FXP-005): commerce: identity, pii, platform, workforce, approvals, accreditation, tenancy, kernel, catalogue, pricing, promotions, seating, orders, payments, ledger, wallet; access: access; operations: inventory, fnb, retail, marketing, queue, maintenance, resources, venuemap, assets, games, rental, transport, subscription, whitelabel, reporting, sync (and control, in the control database, ADR-0039); ticvai_ai: ai (and ai.inbox), read-only on the rest; workers: the schemas its consumers, the outbox relay and the scheduled jobs write, which is every module's.
tasks.linksNothingBecause: roles and grants on every schema, not a table or operation of its own: the owners are listed in its text

tasks.subject: One id type: UUIDv7 from Id.New() in the kernel and in offline-core
tasks.detail: One id type (ADR-0056): `TICVAI.Domain.Identity.Id.New()`, a UUIDv7 `Guid` (RFC 9562) written big-endian so PostgreSQL's uuid order is time order. **The backend repository already has it** (repos/ticvai-docs/setup/backend-patterns.md 3.1: `Guid.NewGuid()` is banned in favour of it; r8 walk fix, CHG-R8WFC-008), so the server side is: confirm the byte order and that no ULID or UUIDv4 is minted anywhere. The offline side is the same generator in each frontend repository whose app creates ids offline (docs/active/frontend-repos.yaml: one GitLab repository per app since 13 October, no shared packages repository), so a till's offline id and a server id sort together. Done when: ids made by the server and by an offline till sort by creation time in PostgreSQL, a .NET-to-TypeScript round-trip test agrees byte for byte, and no ULID string is generated anywhere.
tasks.linksNothingBecause: the id generator in the kernel and offline-core; its text names the files

tasks.subject: Monthly partitions: create three months ahead, detach what retention has expired
tasks.detail: A job in the workers host that keeps monthly range partitions three months ahead on the time-partitioned tables (access.scan_event, platform.outbox, platform.dead_letter, platform.audit_record, ledger.journal_line, marketing.message_dispatch, kernel.inbox; ADR-0056) in every tenant database, and detaches and archives partitions past their retention (ADR-0047). Done when: a new tenant database has partitions three months ahead, a run with the clock moved forward creates the next month, and an expired partition is detached, not deleted row by row. **Order** (R8 blocker FOUNDATION-AI-C31, CHG-R8MIG-020): it needs the first-release migrations of the tables it partitions (MIG-KERNEL, MIG-PLATFORM, MIG-LEDGER, MIG-ACCESS, MIG-MARKETING) applied first, and creates partitions only for the partitioned tables that exist when it runs, so platform.dead_letter, which MIG-PLATFORM-4 creates later, gets its partitions on the first run after that migration; it is a job in the workers host, not a migration file.

tasks.subject: Qdrant cluster in dev and staging: 3 nodes, TLS, snapshots, monitoring
tasks.detail: In **ticvai-infra** (Terraform): a self-hosted 3-node Qdrant cluster in Azure UAE North for staging (ADR-0049), pinned to 1.16 or later, with TLS, JWT RBAC on and the signing key in the cell's Key Vault, snapshot storage in the UAE, and monitoring and alerts on node health, disk and latency. Check Qdrant Hybrid Cloud on our own AKS as an alternative before building. Done when: the cluster survives the loss of one node, a snapshot of a test collection restores into a fresh cluster, and a request without a valid token is refused. **Where the install lives** (the lead, 20 October 2026, r8 cause FOUNDATION-AI-C22, option A): the cluster bootstrap is a second Terraform stage in ticvai-infra, run after the cell module against its AKS cluster with the helm and kubernetes providers; it installs cert-manager (certificates from Let's Encrypt), the ingress and the official Qdrant chart on the qdrant node pool, with TLS and JWT RBAC on. The providers, the chart and cert-manager are on the approved list (setup/dependencies.md). Dev has no cluster (laptops, docker compose); this ticket's cluster is staging's (FOUNDATION-AI-C52).

tasks.subject: Guest web: app shell and design tokens (header, navigation, footer, loader, status, empty and offline patterns, theme)
tasks.detail: In **ticvai-guest-web**. Why: the lead, Chinmay, 21 October 2026: "I wanna get all of those changes out now.." (CHG-R9UI-001, CHG-R9UI-002); the seat page WEB-007 was built with a bare error page and no shell, because no ticket built the app's shell or its tokens and nothing named the approved look. The shell every guest web screen renders inside, identical to the client-approved prototype (sources/designs/guest-rev3-30-september/TICVAI Guest Booking v2.dc.html, rev 3, 30 September 2026): the header and navigation (the brand mark, What's on, the language switch, the account button), the footer, the booking progress bar and breadcrumb, the basket panel where a step shows it, and the state patterns the prototype draws: the turnstile loader (lines 4950-4962), the WEB-029 status card for Error, Sold out and Maintenance (lines 4746-4782; the board frame wireframes/P01 Guest Web.dc.html#web-029), the dashed empty card, the Nothing matched card, the dashed Choose first note, the Sign in to see your account card, the paused action button (Offline, booking is paused) and the video poster frame. The theme is the prototype's CSS variables, written down in handoff/design-tokens/guest-web.yaml (--brand per venue, --accent, --bg, --surface, --ink, --line, --r, --btn-*, --font-h Archivo and --font-b IBM Plex Sans, each with its rule from the prototype's theme()), applied on the root from getPublishedTenantConfig's theme and fonts for the tenant and venue, with dir=rtl for Arabic; no screen hard-codes a colour, font or radius. tasks.subject: Offline journal in packages/offline-core: record, replay and the conflict policies
tasks.detail: In ticvai-frontend packages/offline-core: an append-only journal of sales and scans taken offline, replay on reconnect, and the conflict policies the contracts declare (SD-047). Done when: a POS takes ten cash sales with the network off and all ten reach the server once when it returns. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): the conflict policies are the `x-ticvai-conflict-policy` of each operation the journal records (linked here): `append` for createOrder, createPayment, createCashMovement and validateAccess (nothing is overwritten, so a replayed entry is a new fact, deduplicated by its idempotency key); `lastWriterWins` only where an operation declares it (holdOrder); `serverWins` for everything else (the server's version stands and the till re-reads). Replay goes through `orders#syncOrders` and `access#syncScans` in journal order, each entry with the idempotency key it was taken with. ADR-0013: the catalogue is read locally on every transaction, online or not, and contended inventory sells only from a lease; ADR-0022: the four policies and why the set is closed. **A cash movement** (r8, FOUNDATION-AI-C13): it replays through shift.createCashMovement with its Idempotency-Key and recordedAt; a 409 shift-not-open or lift-exceeds-float on replay is quarantined through recordSyncRejection with kind cashMovement, as a refused sale is.

tasks.subject: Signed catalogue and entitlement bundles, and the lease client
tasks.detail: The signed bundle a till or scanner trades from offline, including entitlements and dynamic access policy for the scanner (SD-052), and the lease each workstation holds (SD-047). Two bundles: the till's signed catalogue bundle (`catalogue#getLatestBundle`, applied whole or not at all and acknowledged with `catalogue#reportBundleApplied`; table catalogue.published_bundle) and the scanner's offline package (`access#getOfflinePackage`). The lease is ADR-0013 section 2: a till holds N units of contended timed capacity for a TTL through `catalogue#acquireInventoryHold` (catalogue.inventory_hold), renewed while the link is up; unsold units return on expiry; seated inventory stays blocked offline (CHG-FXP-005). **Block A takes no standing lease** (ADR-0013 C103; r8, FOUNDATION-AI-C45, GPS-C37): contended timed entry is online-only at the till, and offline the POS-002 sale drawer refuses it and says why (timed entry needs a connection). Done when: offline, a till refuses contended timed entry with that message and sells the rest from its bundle; an offline sale replayed after the hold it relied on expired is accepted and flagged unitsGone for the reconciler, never silently dropped (FOUNDATION-AI-C46); a bundle whose signature does not verify (Ed25519 over contentHash, keys from getBundleSigningKeys with a 7-day grace) is refused whole (FOUNDATION-AI-C14).

tasks.subject: AI gateway, governance decision point and usage metering
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai (Python). One gateway every AI call goes through: capability code calls gateway.run(task, inputs, schema?) and never names a provider (design 3.3). **Routing, in order:** (1) the allowed set: TICVAI's curated catalogue, filtered by the tenant's AI residency class (ADR-0009 amended 2 October, DEC-539): uaeOnly, the default and mandatory for government, bank and health tenants, resolves only to endpoints inside the UAE (Core42 Compass GPT-4.1 mini for the Small tier, Compass GPT-5 for the Strong tier, reached through the existing openaiCompatible provider kind); globalAllowed (a private venue under PDPL Art. 23) resolves to Azure gpt-5-mini / gpt-6-sol Global Standard or the tenant's BYOK provider; onPrem only when a client asks for it, and nothing is built for it in Block A (we host no LLM: Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-004); then by the task's data classification and the governance policy; (2) the task's tier from TICVAI's curated task-to-tier map: a client never picks a model. BYOK accepts any vendor (CHG-FUP-008), is enabled by TICVAI (PLATFORM_AI_MANAGE) for a globalAllowed tenant only, maps each task to that vendor's equivalent model, and is activated by setAiProvider only after testAiProvider's compatibility probes pass (tool calling, structured output, Arabic, context, latency, residency); the key is a per-tenant write-only Key Vault secret shown only by its last four characters; (3) the cascade, Small to Strong only on a checkable signal (schema validation failed twice, retrieval partial), never on a model's self-reported confidence; (4) a circuit breaker per endpoint (opens at 50% errors over 20 calls or p95 above twice the task budget for 60 s; half-open after 30 s) and the class's fallback chain (uaeOnly: Core42 Compass, then OpenAI's UAE region; no LLM is hosted in the cell, so with both down the call goes to degraded mode); a residency refusal is returned, never failed over to another region; (5) degraded mode when nothing answers (search-only, rules-only or 'a person will help'). **Before each call:** the per-request budget and the capability's ceilingBehaviour, maskedFields (fail closed), then the scrubber and input guard of AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD, and a stable-first prompt order for prefix caching. **After it:** structured-output validation, the output guard and the re-fill, an ai.activity row and OpenTelemetry spans with no prompt text. evaluateAiGovernance is an in-process decision point (allow, allow with conditions, prepare only, approval required, escalate, block, with the policy version; design 3.8); getAiUsage meters tokens and spend per tenant; every governed answer writes one ai.decision_record (model, prompt template, policy and knowledge versions; design 3.9). About 12 engineer-days. **setAiProvider and setAiCredential are served here** (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-001): in Block A TICVAI staff enter a tenant's BYOK provider and key under the platform-staff grant on ADM-037 (no tenant self-service yet); the provider is checked against the curated catalogue and the tenant's residency class, and the key goes to the cell's Key Vault, never to a table in clear. About one engineer-day more (13). **Failover, in full** (DEC-539 as amended 3 October; CHG-R1S-001, CHG-R1S-002): a uaeOnly call goes to Core42 Compass by default and falls back only to OpenAI's UAE region (the ae.api.openai.com project); no LLM is hosted in the cell (we host none unless a client asks: Chinmay, 3 October), so with both down it answers in degraded mode. A residency refusal is returned, never failed over to another region, and failover never widens residency (CHG-R1S-016); global endpoints are called statelessly (no Assistants, Threads or Conversations, store=false, no uploads or fine-tuning). Done when: a uaeOnly tenant's call reaches the Compass endpoint and, with Compass forced down, falls back to the OpenAI UAE endpoint, and with both forced down answers in degraded mode, never from a Global endpoint (a test asserts the residency refusal instead of a cross-border call); a BYOK provider that fails a compatibility probe is refused with 409 compatibility-test-required; a tenant over its ceiling gets the capability's ceilingBehaviour; and every call in the test run leaves an ai.activity row, and every governed answer a decision record naming its model, prompt and policy versions.

tasks.subject: PII scrubber in our worker and the provider's safety service in front of every LLM call
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai, for every residency class (ADR-0020 amended 2 October, DEC-542/543; contracts/satellite/ai.yaml AiPolicy.scrubbing, CHG-CSA-003). We host no LLM (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-004): the scrubber runs on the AI GPU node pool in our own cell, Presidio's recognisers on its CPU and the Arabic named-entity model on its GPU beside the embedding model (Chinmay, 4 October, CHG-R11-001), and the guard is the provider-side safety service. Between the gateway's maskedFields step and the provider: (1) detection with Microsoft Presidio (offline) and custom recognisers for Emirates ID numbers, UAE phone numbers, passport numbers, IBANs, Luhn-checked card numbers and email addresses, plus an Arabic named-entity model (CAMeL Tools or an Arabic GLiNER) for Arabic names and places; (2) reversible placeholders ([GUEST_1], [PHONE_1]) whose map lives in the cell for the life of the request only, is never logged and never travels with the prompt, and the reply re-filled before the user sees it; (3) the provider-side safety service (Azure AI Content Safety in UAE North by default, not a guard model of ours) on the prompt before it leaves and on the answer before it is shown, a streamed answer checked as it arrives; a guard model of our own only if a client asks for one; (4) mandatory whatever the residency class: a uaeOnly tenant is scrubbed as well; (5) fails closed: scrubber (or its GPU node) or safety service down means 503 scrubber-unavailable and no provider call; a guard refusal is 422 guard-refused. maskedFields stays the first control; the scrubber is the second, for free text. About 6 engineer-days. Done when: on a test corpus in Arabic and English, a prompt carrying an Emirates ID, a UAE phone number, an IBAN, a card number, an email and an Arabic name reaches the provider stub with placeholders only and no raw value, and the reply comes back re-filled; stopping the scrubber or the safety service refuses the call with 503 and the provider stub receives nothing; a harmful prompt is refused with 422 guard-refused; and the corpus test runs in CI on every gateway change. In ticvai-ai, the scrubber on the AI GPU node pool in our own cell (CHG-R11-001) for every residency class (ADR-0020 amended 2 and 3 October, DEC-542/543, CHG-R1S-002; (3) a second, deterministic pattern pass after Presidio (Emirates ID 784-..., +971 numbers, Luhn card PAN, IBAN, email): any survivor blocks the call (CHG-R1S-016); Presidio's version pinned and recorded on every call (it is community-maintained now: take a release on purpose, after the corpus passes); each call writes its scrub audit (entity counts by type, never values; AiInteraction.scrubAudit); a value planted to slip past Presidio is caught by the pattern pass and blocks the call;

tasks.subject: The baseline-then-learn layer: estimator interface, maturity stages, venue profile, starting patterns
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: the baseline-then-learn layer of design 3.13 (ADR-0051, AI-D16/AI-D17). **One estimator interface per question** (a suggestion kind, a forecast definition, a risk score, a recommendation rank) with three producers behind the same contract: the Prior (the venue AI profile from setAiVenueSettings, a starting pattern per venue type - water park, theme park, family entertainment centre, museum, arena, zoo or aquarium - written by TICVAI from published sources and never from another tenant's data, and the UAE calendar: Sat-Sun weekend, public holidays, Ramadan and Eid by Hijri date, school holidays, summer heat for outdoor venues); the Statistical producer, the tenant's own data pulled toward the prior, (k x prior + n x own mean) / (k + n) with k = coldStart.priorWeightObservations (4 same weekdays by default), re-estimated nightly as a recorded producer version; and the Learned slot, which only an admin's promotion fills (Block B). **Maturity on every answer:** AiMaturity (starting, learning, established, learned) on every Suggestion and AiForecastVersion and one ai.capability_maturity row per question, with the 'Based on' line (your venue profile, UAE calendar, 23 days of your sales), the share of own data and what the next stage needs. A 422 only for a missing setting (AiMissingSettingProblem names the setting and the screen that sets it), never for little history. The weather enters the prior with its Block B adapter. About 15 engineer-days; historical import, the training job and the learned producers continue in Block B. Done when: a new venue with no history gets an answer for every Block A suggestion kind on day one, with stage starting and a Based-on line; after 28 days of seeded sales the stage reads learning and the answer has moved toward the venue's own mean by the formula; a missing setting returns 422 naming it; and a two-tenant test shows no producer reads the other tenant's rows.

tasks.subject: Day-one suggestions for the Block A screens: queue balancing, prep plan, upsell
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: requestSuggestion answers from the baseline (AI-ENGINE-BASELINE) on day one for the kinds the Block A screens call (BO-005 queueBalancing; GST-031 and WEB-044 waitTime and upsell, from the conversation only; prepPlan for the kitchen's production plan), with the upsell baseline from the Promotions relationship map plus business priority (design 3.10, ADR-0052), each answer carrying its maturity stage and Based-on line and recorded through the gateway's decision point. The recommendation runtime itself is Block B (ADR-0052). About 8 engineer-days. Done when: each of those screens gets a suggestion on a freshly seeded venue with no history, none answers 422 for little history, and every answer has a decision record naming its producer and stage.

tasks.subject: Guest concierge: retrieval over the venue's knowledge, answers with sources
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: the guest concierge profile of the one assistant runtime (design 5.10). Knowledge ingest and reindex from the venue's published content into the tenant's Qdrant collection (AI-ENGINE-QDRANT), with embeddings from our own BGE-M3 on the AI GPU node pool in the cell (Chinmay, 4 October, CHG-R11-001: tenant content is never sent to a provider to be embedded) and BGE-M3's dense vectors combined with Qdrant's BM25 sparse index, then reranked by our own reranker on the same node; hybrid retrieval through the single retrieval client (the venue filter always added); answers on the Small tier with sources, the venue's content as the only source, and a reliability category (grounded, partial, conflicting sources, insufficient evidence; design 5.6); the semantic then exact answer cache for FAQ-class answers keyed by tenant, scope path, locale and policy version (threshold 0.95, TTL 60 minutes, never for live numbers; ADR-0034); streaming over sendAiMessage (tokens, then sources and any proposed action; the full message stored); degraded mode: the fallback model, then search-only answers with links, then 'a person will help' (design 3.7). Index lag over 15 minutes alerts (design 4.4). About 8 engineer-days. **getGuestConversation and sendGuestConversationMessage are served here** (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-001): the guest's conversation with the concierge on WEB-044, GST-031 and GST-032, which poll getGuestConversation every 5 s (30 s while the screen is hidden); a sent message is answered through the gateway and stored whole. About one engineer-day more (9). Done when: on the concierge golden set in English and Arabic groundedness and citation accuracy are each at least 95% (design 3.5); a question about another venue's content returns nothing from it; editing a source page invalidates its cached answer; and with the provider stubbed down the guest gets a search-only answer with links, not an error. BGE-M3 and its reranker hosted by us on the AI GPU node pool: Chinmay, 4 October, CHG-R11-001) and the vectors in the tenant's Qdrant collection;

tasks.subject: Qdrant tenancy: a collection and a scoped token per tenant, the retrieval client, erasure and snapshots
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai, on SETUP-QDRANT's cluster (ADR-0049, design 5.8). Collection-per-tenant provisioning at tenant onboarding, per embedding model (t_<tenantId>_<model>) behind the alias tenant_<tenantId> (a model change is a shadow collection, an evaluation and an alias swap); per-tenant HS256 JWT issuance and rotation, scoped to the tenant's collections and alias, signed with the admin API key that only the issuer reads from Key Vault (ticvai-ai never does). The issuer is the workers host (the .NET background-job deployable), which also runs collection, alias, snapshot and offboarding work; the token is read-write ('rw') on the tenant's own collection and alias only, exp 30 days, reissued weekly to Key Vault, and ticvai-ai reloads it when the secret version changes (ADR-0049; the lead, 20 October 2026, r8 cause FOUNDATION-AI-C10); the single retrieval client with no scope parameter that reads the caller's scope from the request and always adds the venue filter (points carry venue_id and scope_path, indexed); dense and sparse named vectors fused by reciprocal rank; erasure by guest or document payload, checked against the point references in ai.chunk_embedding; offboarding that deletes the collections and alias and revokes the token; per-collection snapshots copied to UAE North storage by a CronJob (azcopy, workload identity) and a restore tested per tenant. About 5 engineer-days. Done when: a token for one tenant cannot read another tenant's collection (the store refuses it); a collection-scoped token works through the alias, or the token names both; a venue-scoped question never returns another venue's chunk; an erased guest's points are gone and the check against ai.chunk_embedding proves it; and one tenant's snapshot restores into a fresh collection.

tasks.subject: Guest AI erasure: eraseSubject removes a deleted guest's index rows and search points, with the counts that prove it
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai, beside AI-ENGINE-QDRANT, whose erasure by guest payload it calls. **Built in Block A by the lead's decision** (20 October 2026, "Accepting both as recommended", CHG-R8ERA-001): Block A indexes support cases (marketing.case, which carry the guest's subjectId) through reindexSource, so a deleted guest's case text would otherwise stay searchable until a later block. eraseSubject (contracts/satellite/ai.yaml, POST /internal/subjects/{subjectId}/ai-erasure) is an internal operation: serviceAuth over the cell's mTLS, no user permission, called only by Identity's erasure job for a guest whose pii.subject row it has tombstoned (deleteGuestAccount, CHG-R8ERA-002). For the subject, in this order: delete the ai.index_entry rows and the ai.chunk_embedding rows with that subject_id in one transaction, then the Qdrant points whose payload subjectId is the subject, by payload filter (which also catches a point whose row went first); then count what is left in both stores. It answers 200 with subjectId, indexEntriesRemoved, chunksRemoved, pointsRemoved, rowsLeft and pointsLeft; zero left is the proof the erasure keeps. A subject with nothing indexed, or already erased, answers 200 with zeros (never a 404 or 409), so Identity's retry is always safe; the Idempotency-Key replays the first answer. Qdrant unreachable: the rows are still removed in their transaction and the call answers 502 provider-connection-failed, so Identity retries and the retry removes the points. It writes only ai.index_entry and ai.chunk_embedding (their subject_id columns exist: V0104, V0108; no new migration) and logs no guest text. About 2 engineer-days. Done when: a guest with an indexed support case is erased and the call answers rowsLeft 0 and pointsLeft 0 with the removed counts above 0; semanticSearch no longer returns that case's text, and another guest's points and rows are untouched; a second call for the same subject answers 200 with zeros; with Qdrant forced down the call answers 502 provider-connection-failed with the rows gone, and the next call removes the points and answers zero left; and a guest's or a staff member's token cannot call it (serviceAuth only).

tasks.subject: Help me choose: suggested question sets from the product catalogue
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: Help me choose suggested from the catalogue (design 3.11, decided 29 September; capability C7 at autonomy 'suggest'). Rules first: read each guest-sellable product's category, subcategory, segment tags (level, audience), minimum height and age, duration, price band and language through the catalogue API with the venue's permissions; pick the one or two attributes that split the products most evenly, dropping any where one answer leaves nothing bookable (deterministic: the same catalogue gives the same questions); map each answer to a product, a category or a flow. The Small tier writes the question, answer titles and one-liners in the tenant's languages from the attributes only, never guest data; with the model unavailable the attribute names are used as they are. The draft is saved through proposeGuidedChoice (source aiSuggested, suggestionRef) with a decision record of the inputs, the split each question makes and the model and prompt versions. Publishing is publishGuidedChoice by a person holding TENANT_PUBLISH; nothing is published automatically. A withdrawn mapped product, or new products no answer reaches, raise a new suggestion and never rewrite the published version. About 4 engineer-days. Done when: the same catalogue run twice gives the same questions; the draft lands with source aiSuggested and a decision record; with the model stubbed down a usable draft still lands with attribute names; nothing is live until a person publishes; and withdrawing a mapped product raises a new suggestion.

tasks.subject: Content translation English and Arabic for the CMS
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: proposeTranslations for CMS content, English to Arabic and Arabic to English (and the other locales a tenant enables), on the Small tier with the tenant glossary in the cached prompt prefix so brand terms and register hold (research T03); placeholders, markup and links preserved; scrubbed and guarded like every call (AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD). The result is an AI draft on the field until an operator saves it, and is never published automatically. With the model unavailable the field is left blank and marked missing, never filled with the source text. About 3 engineer-days. Done when: an English CMS page gets an Arabic draft that keeps every glossary term and placeholder; the draft stays a draft until an operator saves it; and with the provider stubbed down the field reads missing, not English.

tasks.subject: Venue-map proposals: walkways from a raster plan and labels for extracted shapes
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: the AI side of proposeWalkways and proposeVenueLabels for the venue-map import that ships in r1 (CHG-RONEC-001; BO-093 Map Import & Labelling, BO-094; ADR-0069; Chinmay, 4 October, CHG-AIPH-002). The operations' endpoints and their writes are the back-end tasks SVC-AI-AI-3 (proposeWalkways) and SVC-AI-AI-1 (proposeVenueLabels); this task is the model work behind them. Walkways: only for a raster plan (a scan, a photograph, an illustrated map, a scanned PDF read through the OCR step), where there is no geometry to subtract; where the import found hand-marked paths (VenueMapImportJob.handMarkedPaths) the proposal follows the marks, one segment per marked stretch between junctions with basis handMarked and a confidence for how cleanly the stroke was traced, a gap in a mark proposed as two segments and never bridged; otherwise basis auto or seen, with a confidence per segment, low-confidence segments shown and never filtered out. Labels: read the shapes venue-map.importVenueGeometry already extracted (never the drawing itself) and propose what each one is (kind and name), using scanned text near a shape as a hint (ocrHint says which text was used); text alone never creates a point or raises a proposal above what the shape supports. Both write ai.proposed_action through the gateway's decision point and stop: nothing is a path or a label until an operator accepts it, segment by segment (venue-map.acceptWalkwayProposals) and proposal by proposal (acceptVenueLabelProposals), on BO-093. The proposals are scrubbed and guarded like every call (AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD) and read only the tenant's own map and knowledge collection (ADR-0020; the label proposals read the venue's Qdrant collection, AI-ENGINE-QDRANT). An evaluation set of TICVAI's own drawings (raster plans with and without hand marks, CAD exports with labelled and unlabelled layers, Arabic and English text) joins the harness (AI-ENGINE-EVAL). With the provider down the import still completes: no proposals are raised and BO-093 says the AI proposals are unavailable, never an empty network presented as complete. About 2.5 engineer-days. Done when: a raster plan with hand-marked paths gets one proposed segment per marked stretch with basis handMarked and its confidence, and a gap stays a gap; a raster plan without marks gets segments with a confidence each, the low ones shown; extracted shapes get kind and name proposals that cite their ocrHint where they used scanned text; nothing is applied until an operator accepts it, segment by segment and proposal by proposal, on BO-093; it answers through the AI gateway with the scrubber and the guard on, its evaluation set passes the gate of docs/architecture/ai-system-design.md 3.5, it degrades as 3.7 says when its provider is down, and a peer AI engineer has reviewed it.

tasks.subject: The planner agent on top of the rules planner
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: the planner agent on top of the rules planner in venue-map (design 2.3 and 7; MOB-6). The schedule is solved deterministically (OR-Tools CP-SAT over show times, opening hours, walking times and configured capacity; research T04) and the Small tier reads the guest's intent and writes the why. The agent works only through the plan operations as the guest (the itinerary kind of requestSuggestion and its plan tools), never writes venuemap.visit_plan itself, and is grounded in each day's venue: it proposes only what that day's tools return, and a wish the venue cannot meet is answered from VisitPlan.unmatchedPreferences. When AI is off or fails it falls back to the rules plan, never to an error. About 8 engineer-days. Done when: a refinement in chat (add lunch at one, skip the coasters) produces a valid plan through the plan tools that respects show times and capacity; a request for something at another venue is answered from unmatchedPreferences and updateVisitPlan refuses the point (422 point-not-at-day-venue); and with the model stubbed down the guest gets the rules plan.

tasks.subject: Evaluation harness and the promotion alert
tasks.detail: In ticvai-ai: the evaluation harness and release pipeline of design 3.5. Golden sets per capability in the repository (Arabic, English and code-mixed cases, plus permission and tenant-isolation cases such as 'show revenue for another tenant'), run by runAiEvaluation; isolation and permission cases must pass 100% and a single failure blocks the release. Scores land in AiModel.taskFitness with the task's band; a model bound outside it returns fitnessWarnings on setAiProvider (warn, never block; AI-D18). The Arabic golden set decides between Compass GPT-4.1 mini and GPT-4.1 Arabic (Seraj) for the uaeOnly Small tier (ADR-0009 amended), and a BYOK vendor's model enters the curated map only after passing the task's set. Release stages draft, offline evaluation, shadow, canary, production, with rollback as a pointer switch; the backtest runner the learned producers will use; and a shadow producer that passes its promotion gate raises one ai.governance_alert of kind promotionReady and a P09 tile, and never switches itself (AI-D16). About 5 engineer-days. Done when: CI runs the harness on every Block A AI answer type (concierge, Help me choose wording, translations, planner, day-one suggestions) and blocks a merge on any isolation failure or a regression against the previous release; a model scored outside its band returns fitnessWarnings; and a seeded shadow producer that passes its gate raises exactly one promotionReady alert and changes nothing live.

tasks.subject: Per-tenant request budgets: a token bucket per tenant and audience, and a load-aware share per replica
tasks.detail: ADR-0064 (accepted 1 October), in the kernel middleware of the commerce, access and operations hosts: a token bucket per tenant and audience (guest/public, staff, service, partner) with counts shared through Azure Managed Redis, sustained rate and a 2x burst for 10 seconds from the tenant's plan, asked of Platform with the `subscription#tenantRequestLimits` service query over its route GET /internal/tenant-request-limits?tenantId= (`getTenantRequestLimits`, serviceAuth; ADAM CR-491), cached per tenant for 60 seconds, a tenant with no current contract getting the platform default held as per-cell configuration under the key `RequestLimits:Tenant:PlatformDefault` (ADAM CR-490); one tenant held to 25% of a replica's request slots only while the replica is above 70% of its limit; shedding guest and public first, staff and service last (ADR-0032); 429 with Retry-After and the RateLimit-* headers; if Redis is unavailable each replica falls back to its own in-process buckets (the limit divided by the replica count). Done when: in a test with two tenants on one replica, the busy tenant gets the whole replica while the other is quiet, is held to 25% of the slots once the replica passes 70% while the quiet tenant's requests still succeed, a guest burst never spends a till's staff budget, and stopping Redis leaves requests served under the in-process limits. Contract (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): the plan's limits are `Plan.requestLimits` in contracts/satellite/subscription.yaml, read through the `tenantRequestLimits` query of that contract over Platform's service route, never `subscription#getPlan` (the control database is not the cell's; r8 walk fix, CHG-R8WFC-008); the refusal is the shared `rate-limited` problem (429) of contracts/shared/common.yaml with `Retry-After` and the RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers it defines.

tasks.subject: Field encryption in the kernel: per-tenant data and blind-index keys behind one interface (ADR-0063 action 6)
tasks.detail: ADR-0063 action 6 (ADAM CR-271, CR-283; the lead, 29 October 2026): one Application abstraction in the kernel that encrypts, decrypts and blind-indexes a value for the current tenant (ITenantContext), so no module calls Key Vault itself. Interface: Encrypt(plaintext) returns the stored string, Decrypt(stored) returns the plaintext, BlindIndex(value) returns 64 lowercase hex characters (HMAC-SHA-256); all three act for the current tenant only. Keys: per tenant, a data key (AES-256-GCM) and a blind-index key (HMAC-SHA-256), created when the tenant is provisioned (or on first use) and wrapped by the tenant's HSM-backed Key Vault key (ADR-0063 section 5, amended 14 October 2026); unwrapped keys live only in memory, cached per tenant, and are never logged or stored unwrapped. Where the wrapped keys are kept (ADAM CR-339; the lead, 30 October 2026): the tenant database's platform.tenant_field_key (purpose dataKey or blindIndexKey, key_version, wrapped_key, wrapping_key_id naming the Key Vault key and its version, state active, decryptOnly or retired, created_at, rotated_at; one row per purpose and version, one active row per purpose), read and written by the kernel alone, which the architecture test covers as it covers the Key Vault client. A missing key is created at provisioning or on first use with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and then read again, so two hosts creating it at once end up with one key; it is unwrapped with the key version its wrapping_key_id names. The two tables are CR339-FIELD-KEY-TABLES-DB's (Hrushikant Patkar); until that lands, build behind the key-store abstraction. The stored form names the key version, enc:v<version>:<base64url(nonce | ciphertext | tag)>, so a value written under an older key still decrypts after rotation. Rotation (CR-339): rotating the data key adds a new active row and moves the old one to decryptOnly, and enc:v<version> says which row decrypts. Rotating the blind-index key re-hashes only a blind index the server can decrypt, today marketing.guest_device.token_fingerprint (from token_ciphertext): its progress is a row of platform.blind_index_rehash (column_name as schema.table.column, from_version, to_version, last_id, started_at, finished_at; one row per column and target version), and a lookup on that column tries both versions only while its row is unfinished. The other tenant blind indexes hash a token the server never keeps (marketing.subscription.unsubscribe_token, orders.payment_link.token, orders.wallet_pass.authentication_token, orders.ticket_transfer.claim_token), so they cannot be re-hashed: their old version stays decryptOnly, and a lookup tries the active version and then each decryptOnly one, newest first, for as long as a token made under it can still be presented, the rule ADR-0063 already gives API client secrets. The kernel's list of blind-index columns is the contracts' x-ticvai-secret: blind-index columns of the tenant database; tenancy.device_credential.fingerprint is not one. One tenant's keys never decrypt or match another tenant's values. Key Vault unreachable with no cached key: the call fails with the shared 503 problem, never a fall back to plaintext or an unkeyed hash. TOTP secrets (CR-173) use the same per-tenant data key: ADR-0063's per-tenant key is the rule, and CR-173's per-cell key wording is superseded. Infrastructure (Hrushikant Patkar): the HSM-backed Key Vault per cell and the hosts' managed identity access to it, with soft-delete and purge protection on, so a key version that a row names, a row in a restored backup included, is never purged (CR-339). The operations that wait for it: registerGuestDevice (push token, CR-086), enrolMfaMethod, verifyMfaChallenge and verifyMfaEnrolment (CR-173), recordStorefrontSessionEvents (CR-107). Done when: round-trip tests pass; two tenants cannot decrypt or blind-index-match each other's values; a data-key rotation test decrypts old values; a blind-index rotation re-hashes guest_device.token_fingerprint with its lookup trying both versions until its platform.blind_index_rehash row is finished, and a one-way index still matches a token made under a decryptOnly version; a blind index is stable within a tenant and different across tenants; no module outside the kernel references the Key Vault client.

tasks.subject: Service sign-in between deployables inside a cell: workload identity, token validation, the caller's context (ADR-0073)
tasks.detail: The serviceAuth scheme the contracts name (ADAM CR-281; the lead, 29 October 2026), so one deployable (commerce, access, operations, workers, ticvai-ai; ADR-0055) can call another's operation or service query inside a cell; nothing built it before (CR-174, CR-241, CR-281). 1. ADR-0073 first, for the lead's approval: how each deployable proves who it is (its own workload identity), mTLS between them inside the cell, and how the callee validates the call. 2. Validation: the callee accepts a call only with a valid token for itself (issuer the cell's identity, audience the callee deployable, not expired); anything else is 401 with the shared problem. 3. The caller's context: the caller sends the tenant, scope and subject of the request it acts for, and the callee sets ITenantContext from them only after the token is valid; a caller acting for no person (a job, a consumer) runs at the scope the route's contract names. 4. Client side: one shared kernel client that every x-ticvai-read-via query with route service, and every serviceAuth call, goes through, so no module builds its own. The operations that wait for it: endGuestDeviceSessions, recordConsentIdentifier, updateGuestSubjectDetails, requeueDeadLetter and listCellEndpoints (CR-281), not setAnalyticsProvider or setMaintenanceMode, which waited only for tenancy#activeVenues and now ask it in process (ADAM CR-343; the lead, 30 October 2026), the follow-ups CR-174, CR-241, CR-275 and CR-277 left for after service sign-in, and the operations that read another deployable's data over the service route. Done when: in a test with two deployables, a valid call succeeds with the caller's tenant and scope in the callee's context; a missing, expired or wrong-audience token is 401; no shared SQL is used between them (ADR-0055 rule 4).

tasks.subject: Redis in the kernel: the client, keyed state with expiry and take-once, and the rule when Redis is down
tasks.detail: The Redis client and one small Application abstraction over it (ADAM CR-282; the lead, 29 October 2026). The contracts already keep SSO sign-in state (cache:sso-state:<state>), Identity's guest session registry (ADR-0004) and the session cache (cache:resolution) in Redis, and the repository had no client. Client: StackExchange.Redis, one connection multiplexer per host, registered in the kernel. Abstraction: Set(key, value, expiry), Get(key), TakeOnce(key) (atomic read-and-delete, GETDEL) and Delete(key); every key is prefixed with the tenant id, so tenants never share a key. Connection: one setting per cell; Hrushikant Patkar provisions Azure Managed Redis per cell and its access (managed identity, or a secret in Key Vault). Redis down: take-once state and the guest session registry fail closed with the shared 503 problem and Retry-After, with no in-process fallback, because single use must hold across replicas; the session cache falls back to the database read. KERNEL-TENANT-LIMITS keeps its own in-process fallback and uses this client (ADR-0064). The operations that wait for it: startSsoAuthorization, completeSsoAuthorization and endGuestDeviceSessions (with KERNEL-SERVICE-AUTH). Done when: TakeOnce succeeds once and only once under concurrent calls; expiry is honoured; two tenants' identical keys do not collide; stopping Redis gives 503 on SSO start and complete and still serves getCurrentSession from the database.

tasks.subject: Device sign-in (deviceAuth): validate the enrolled credential and act at the device's workstation
tasks.detail: The deviceAuth scheme decided on 20 October 2026 (APPROVALS-TENANCY-C27 option A, CHG-R8SPN-030; ADAM CR-284, the lead, 29 October 2026): a device proves itself with the credential its enrolment issued (tenancy.device_credential), and acts at the scope of the workstation it is bound to; nothing built it before. Validation: the presented credential is checked against tenancy.device_credential, as that table and CHG-R8SPN-030 describe it: it must match, not be revoked and not be expired; otherwise the answer is 401 with the shared problem. Context: ITenantContext gets the device's tenant and the scope path of its bound workstation, with no principal; the device id is available to the operation. Revocation takes effect on the next call (no long-lived cache of a credential's validity). The operation that waits for it: recordDeviceHeartbeat. Done when: an enrolled device's call succeeds at its workstation's scope; an unknown, revoked or expired credential is 401; a device bound to one venue's workstation cannot act at another venue.

tasks.subject: Alerts on one tenant's share of its connection pool and on max_connections
tasks.detail: ADR-0064 item 4: per-tenant pool caps stay, and two alerts watch them: one tenant holding more than 60% of its pool for five minutes, and the instance passing 80% of max_connections; plus a dashboard panel of 429s per tenant and audience from KERNEL-TENANT-LIMITS. Done when: a load run that holds one tenant's pool fires the first alert after five minutes naming the tenant, and opening connections past 80% of max_connections fires the second. Where the numbers come from (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): one tenant's share is the server connections in use for that tenant database, sv_active plus sv_used from PgBouncer's SHOW POOLS, against the database's pool_size from SHOW DATABASES (what ADR-0032 and ADR-0040 say is monitored), with cl_waiting above 0 as a second signal (r8, FOUNDATION-AI-C24); the instance figure is the count of pg_stat_activity against max_connections; both are scraped into the Prometheus-compatible metrics of SETUP-OBS and alert through its Azure Monitor action group, labelled with tenant_id and cell. The pooler is Azure's built-in PgBouncer (r8, FOUNDATION-AI-C53, lead 20 October 2026): Terraform sets pgbouncer.enabled on the Flexible Server (port 6432), and its statistics are read through the admin console on 6432 by a monitoring role with no data access. This alert is the PgBouncer saturation alert of docs/architecture/observability.md: this ticket builds it and its scrape, and PLATFORM-OBSERVE does not build a second one. Thresholds are proposed, client to confirm (that document's alert table).
tasks.linksNothingBecause: alerts on PgBouncer and PostgreSQL statistics; the thresholds and where they come from are in its text

tasks.subject: The on-sale waiting room: Redis positions, the cached page, the release controller, admission tokens
tasks.detail: ADR-0066 (accepted 1 October; B1, or Block A if an on-sale is booked in Block A): enterWaitingRoom gives a position from a Redis counter with no database write; the static branded waiting page is served from Front Door's cache and polls getWaitingRoomPosition; a release controller admits guests per second from the health of commerce (latency and the 429 rate, ADR-0064); an admitted guest gets a short-lived signed token (tenant, performance, expiry, unique id; key in Key Vault) that middleware checks by signature, with no database read, on addCartLine and acquireInventoryHold from guest channels only (till, kiosk and workstation holds are exempt, amendment of 1 October); activation follows the performance's onSaleFrom/onSaleTo or setWaitingRoomSetting. Done when: with the room on, a guest cart hold without a token is refused 403 admission-required, one with a valid token succeeds, a forged or expired token or one for another performance is refused, a till hold needs no token, and the release rate drops when commerce latency rises.

tasks.subject: Load test the waiting room at 50,000 arrivals in the burst environment
tasks.detail: ADR-0066 item 4 as amended on 6 October (the client's sizing benchmarks, CHG-R4-017), before the first large sale: 50,000 simultaneous arrivals in the opening seconds against a burst environment (ADR-0035) with the waiting room on, the sale behind the room held at 3,000 concurrent B2C users and then stepped above it to show the benchmark is not a limit (docs/active/block-test-strategy.md, Load scenarios), recording position latency, the Front Door cache hit rate, the release rate the controller holds, commerce p95 and 429s, and the relay lag while admitted guests buy (ADR-0058 amendment: 3,500 events a second). Done when: all 50,000 get a position without a database write, admitted guests buy with commerce p95 inside its target at 3,000 concurrent and above, no cart hold succeeds without a token, and the results are recorded against the sizing figures.

tasks.subject: One admission rule format, two evaluators: .NET and TypeScript proven equal by shared test vectors
tasks.detail: ADR-0068 (accepted 1 October; B1, with the scanner): the closed JSON rule format (AdmissionRule, AdmissionCondition; conditionRule on access.dynamic_policy versions) evaluated by validateAccess online in .NET and by the gate offline in TypeScript (packages/offline-core) against the same active policy version that getOfflinePackage carries; each scan_event records the policy version that decided it. Done when: one set of test vectors runs in CI against both evaluators and they agree on every vector, a rule the format cannot express is refused when the policy is saved, and an offline scan and an online scan of the same credential under the same policy version give the same decision.

tasks.subject: Identity verification for accreditation: UAE Pass and ICP
tasks.detail: 2 October (Chinmay, DEC-457): UAE Pass sign-in/verification and ICP (Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security) document checks for accreditation applicants, alongside manual review. Needs client access to both (external dependencies register). Done when: an applicant verified through UAE Pass shows the verified identity on the reviewer workspace, and an ICP check result is recorded on the application.

tasks.subject: Same numbers test: till, back-office and Analytics reports agree
tasks.detail: 2 October (Chinmay, DEC-559, prevention of CHG-FIN-006): an automated comparison of the same measure (takings, gross sales, net revenue, refunds) for the same period and scope on the till report (POS-008), the back-office report and the Analytics (P16) dashboard; fails when they differ. Done when: the test runs in CI against the seeded demo tenant.

tasks.subject: BOCA ticket and wristband printing: FGL driver behind the ticketPrinter port
tasks.detail: In the device app (ADR-0015 Tier A; the client confirmed BOCA and sent its documents on 5 October 2026, sources/client/2026-10-05-allam-boca-printer.md; CHG-R4-002). Implement the ticketPrinter port of handoff/integration-register.md for BOCA in FGL: render a ticket or wristband from the ticket designer's layout (updateTicketTemplate, listTicketTemplates; the same layout printTicketProof previews) to FGL: text, fonts including Arabic (as a bitmap where FGL needs it), barcode and QR, the logo bitmap and the cut; printer status and errors (paper out, jam, offline) reported so the kiosk shows KSK-010 Print failure and the POS its reprint path (reprintOrder, POS-026); reprint; and a virtual (emulated) BOCA printer for the tests and CI. RFID encoding on the BOCA Lemur is built behind a flag, off, until the client confirms its scope (Decisions Register, pending). The hardware validation runs on the real unit when it reaches the India office. Done when: a kiosk sale and a POS sale print a ticket and a wristband from the designer layout on the emulator with the same output as the designer's print preview, print failures reach KSK-010 and POS-026, and the hardware check is listed as pending the device.

tasks.subject: Products wave 1: forward migration of the new catalogue and marketing tables and the session's working venue
tasks.detail: Spec: the contracts at the release tag in ADAM (CHG-R8PRD-002 to 011), from the 16 October 2026 minutes (sources/mom/TICVAI_MoM_2026-10-16_TicketingConfig_Wireframes_Plan.md). One forward migration, additive, in the tenant database: catalogue.product_tag, catalogue.product_channel_text, catalogue.product_owner_form, catalogue.product_sale_permission and marketing.form_submission_sale_link, each with the columns, keys and references its contract schema declares (ProductTag, ProductChannelTexts, ProductOwnerForm, ProductSalePermissionRule, FormSubmissionSaleLink: x-ticvai-unique, x-ticvai-unique-together, x-ticvai-unique-nulls, x-ticvai-required-when, x-ticvai-references) and row security on scope_path like every tenant table; and the column identity.session.working_venue_id (SessionVenue.workingVenueId; venue_id is not touched). Seeding of catalogue.product_tag, per venue (CHG-R8PRD-010, -011), so every stored value maps to exactly one tag: (1) take every segment_tags value of the venue's products and every segmentTags value of the venue's Help me choose answer filters (whitelabel.guided_choice_answer), trim it, drop empty values; (2) its key is lower(value); values with one key are one tag; every tag's name is the original value of the first of them (product id order, then answer id order), trimmed and cut to 80 characters; (3) literal codes first: a key matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)*$ and at most 64 characters is the tag's code; then derived codes, in key order: every run of characters outside a-z, 0-9 and / becomes one hyphen, hyphens are trimmed at the ends of each /-segment, empty segments are dropped, an empty result becomes tag (the base); the candidate is the base cut to 64 characters; while the candidate is taken in the venue, try suffix n = 2, 3 and so on, the candidate being the base cut to 64 minus the length of -n, followed by -n; after any cut, trailing / and - are trimmed before a suffix is added, so every derived code fits 64 characters and matches the code pattern; (4) each product's segment_tags and each answer filter's segmentTags is rewritten to its tags' codes, in the original order, duplicates removed (the answer rows are WhiteLabel's: its owner reviews that part). A second run finds every value already a code and changes nothing. Done when: applied to a database at the previous state it creates exactly these, a second run changes nothing, and the result matches the package's derived DDL for them at the release tag.
