tasks.subject: r8: bring your local database to r8 (renamed tables, new columns)
tasks.detail: Why: the lead, 20 October 2026: every developer runs a local database, and r8 changes it. What changed: r8 brings the tenant database to the names the contracts use and adds what the contracts gained since r1. V0103a and V0105a rename 15 tables and move 4 into the sync schema (19 in all), with 20 column renames and the keys, indexes and row-level security policies named for them: catalogue.inventory_hold is now catalogue.inventory_reservation, wallet.hold is wallet.fund_reservation, the wallet *_rules tables are wallet.channel_rule, funding_rule, risk_rule_set and transfer_rule, seating.seat_hold and seat_hold_item are seating.seat_reservation and seat_reservation_item, inventory.item is inventory.inventory_item, inventory.stock_reservation is inventory.stock_earmark, and platform.guest_link, cross_region_entitlement, wallet_authorisation and dsar_request move to sync; columns such as platform.workstation.cash_drawer_limit become deposit_box_limit_amount. V0108 adds 18 tables, 95 columns and their keys and indexes, and widens two CHECKs (inventory.stock_earmark.source_type gains retailReservation, seating.seat_reservation.status gains sold); V0109 adds the foreign keys into the renamed tables, NOT VALID. In the control database V0108 adds 19 tables and 4 columns and V0109 2 keys and an index. Every rename is a guarded block (it does nothing when the old name is not there or the new one already is), so each file can run twice. The files, in this order (every file since r7; apply any of them your database's platform.schema_version does not list yet, in name order, and skip none): tenant database: backend/tenant/V0103a__names_early_after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/tenant/V0105a__names_early_after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/tenant/V0107__names_after_r1_20261019.sql, backend/tenant/V0108__after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/tenant/V0109__names_after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/tenant/V0110__after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/tenant/V0111__names_after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/tenant/V0112__after_r1_20261021.sql, backend/tenant/V0113__after_r1_20261021.sql (r9), backend/tenant/V0114__after_r1_20261022.sql (r9), backend/tenant/V0115__names_after_r1_20261022.sql (r9); control database: backend/control/V0107__names_after_r1_20261019.sql, backend/control/V0108__after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/control/V0109__names_after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/control/V0110__after_r1_20261020.sql, backend/control/V0112__after_r1_20261021.sql. V0107 renames columns, V0110 and V0111 add the columns and keys the r8 fixes added, and V0112 those of the re-walk fixes (wallet.credit_lot.order_line_id, retail.sale_line.order_line_id, the wider product kind and wallet adjustment kind CHECKs; in control, the licence add-on's removal record). How to apply: with psql, file by file in that order, against your own local databases, from the package root: `psql "$TENANT_DB" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f backend/tenant/V0103a__names_early_after_r1_20261020.sql`, then each of the other tenant files the same way, then the five control files against "$CONTROL_DB". These are the package's files, not ours: each records itself in platform.schema_version, so they are not copied into db/tenant or db/control and not run through SqlMigrationRunner (setup/backend-patterns.md section 3.4); your migrations in our repository stay as they are, and the [DB] ticket that creates a table carries the same change. Tenant V0108 and control V0110 alter tables your database may not have yet: if one stops on `... does not exist`, run that file again with `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=0` and read the errors. Exactly six errors are accepted, all `does not exist`, on a database our team's repository built: in tenant V0108, `relation "marketing.privacy_exception" does not exist` three times (a table the repository has not built yet) and `column "scope_path" does not exist` twice (platform.outbox_sequence keeps the shape our repository's migration 240 gives it, CR-166); in control V0110, `relation "control.onboarding_application" does not exist` once (a table the repository has not built yet). Any other error: write it in a comment here and stop. Then run them all again: the second run changes nothing (for V0108 and V0110, the same lines and nothing else). One command does it: tools/db/apply-r8.sh in the package, which runs each file as one transaction and retries only tenant V0108 and control V0110 statement by statement, accepting only those six errors. It reads the files from a `sql` folder beside it: copy tools/db/apply-r8.sh and the thirteen r8 files above (all but the files marked r9) into a folder of your own as `apply-r8.sh`, `sql/tenant/<file>.sql` and `sql/control/<file>.sql`, then run `bash apply-r8.sh <host> <user> <tenant_db> <control_db> <log folder>` with PGPASSWORD (and PGPORT if not 5432, PGBIN if psql is not in C:/Program Files/PostgreSQL/18/bin) in the environment. It runs every file twice; the second pass changes nothing. Then apply the files marked r9 in the list above, in name order, each with `psql -1 -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f`, twice: each applies with no error either time, every statement in them is guarded. V0113 (r9, CR-166) takes away the scope_path, its index and its scope policy V0108 gave platform.outbox_sequence where V0108 could add them, so the table has the shape our repository's migration 240 gives it (aggregate_id and last_sequence, read, inserted and updated by any connection holding a grant, never deleted); on a database our repository built it changes nothing. V0114 (r9: CR-182, CR-184, CR-191, CR-196) makes platform.idempotency_record unique on (operation_id, idempotency_key) with status completed only (a NOT VALID check: rows already there are not rechecked), re-applies the row-level security of orders.cart, orders.sales_order, orders.order_line and orders.order_event so a guest reads its own cart and orders (staff still by venue or scope) and of the 21 tables under them, and grants commerce SELECT on access.entitlement and access.scan_event where the commerce role exists. V0115 (r9: CR-146) puts five foreign keys in the reference's form: rental.booking's deposit key now points at orders.payment, platform.configuration_profile's primary key is widened (its old key and the keys onto it replaced first) and platform.profile_deployment's key onto it is on (profile_id, version), venuemap.visit_plan's subject key points at pii.subject, and platform.workstation gains its key onto configuration_profile, each added NOT VALID and doing nothing where the key is already the reference's. How to check (in psql, each answers true): `select to_regclass('catalogue.inventory_reservation') is not null and to_regclass('catalogue.inventory_hold') is null;` `select to_regclass('wallet.fund_reservation') is not null and to_regclass('wallet.hold') is null;` `select to_regclass('seating.seat_reservation') is not null and to_regclass('seating.seat_hold') is null;` `select to_regclass('sync.guest_link') is not null and to_regclass('platform.guest_link') is null;` (a check whose new and old names are both null is a table your database never had: that is fine), and `select version from platform.schema_version where version like 'V01%' order by version;` lists the number of every tenant file above in the tenant database, and of every control file above in control (an older V0100 to V0102 may be there too). Done when: applied and checked, or, if your local database has none of the tables these files touch, close this task as not needed with a one-line comment saying so.

V0103a and V0105a rename 15 tables and move 4 into the sync schema (19 in all), with 20 column renames and the keys, indexes and row-level security policies named for them: catalogue.inventory_hold is now catalogue.inventory_reservation, wallet.hold is wallet.fund_reservation, the wallet *_rules tables are wallet.channel_rule, funding_rule, risk_rule_set and transfer_rule, seating.seat_hold and seat_hold_item are seating.seat_reservation and seat_reservation_item, inventory.item is inventory.inventory_item, inventory.stock_reservation is inventory.stock_earmark, and platform.guest_link, cross_region_entitlement, wallet_authorisation and dsar_request move to sync; columns such as platform.workstation.cash_drawer_limit become deposit_box_limit_amount. V0108 adds 18 tables, 95 columns and their keys and indexes, and widens two CHECKs (inventory.stock_earmark.source_type gains retailReservation, seating.seat_reservation.status gains sold); V0109 adds the foreign keys into the renamed tables, NOT VALID. In the control database V0108 adds 19 tables and 4 columns and V0109 2 keys and an index. V0107 renames columns, V0110 and V0111 add the columns and keys the r8 fixes added, and V0112 those of the re-walk fixes (wallet.credit_lot.order_line_id, retail.sale_line.order_line_id, the wider product kind and wallet adjustment kind CHECKs; in control, the licence add-on's removal record). How to apply: with psql, file by file in that order, against your own local databases, from the package root: `psql "$TENANT_DB" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f backend/tenant/V0103a__names_early_after_r1_20261020.sql`, then each of the other tenant files the same way, then the five control files against "$CONTROL_DB". These are the package's files, not ours: each records itself in platform.schema_version, so they are not copied into db/tenant or db/control and not run through SqlMigrationRunner (setup/backend-patterns.md section 3.4); your migrations in our repository stay as they are, and the [DB] ticket that creates a table carries the same change. Tenant V0108 and control V0110 alter tables your database may not have yet: if one stops on `... does not exist`, run that file again with `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=0` and read the errors. Exactly six errors are accepted, all `does not exist`, on a database our team's repository built: in tenant V0108, `relation "marketing.privacy_exception" does not exist` three times (a table the repository has not built yet) and `column "scope_path" does not exist` twice (platform.outbox_sequence keeps the shape our repository's migration 240 gives it, CR-166); in control V0110, `relation "control.onboarding_application" does not exist` once (a table the repository has not built yet). Any other error: write it in a comment here and stop. Then run them all again: the second run changes nothing (for V0108 and V0110, the same lines and nothing else). One command does it: tools/db/apply-r8.sh in the package, which runs each file as one transaction and retries only tenant V0108 and control V0110 statement by statement, accepting only those six errors. It reads the files from a `sql` folder beside it: copy tools/db/apply-r8.sh and the thirteen r8 files above (all but the files marked r9) into a folder of your own as `apply-r8.sh`, `sql/tenant/<file>.sql` and `sql/control/<file>.sql`, then run `bash apply-r8.sh <host> <user> <tenant_db> <control_db> <log folder>` with PGPASSWORD (and PGPORT if not 5432, PGBIN if psql is not in C:/Program Files/PostgreSQL/18/bin) in the environment. It runs every file twice; the second pass changes nothing. Then apply the files marked r9 in the list above, in name order, each with `psql -1 -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f`, twice: each applies with no error either time, every statement in them is guarded. V0113 (r9, CR-166) takes away the scope_path, its index and its scope policy V0108 gave platform.outbox_sequence where V0108 could add them, so the table has the shape our repository's migration 240 gives it (aggregate_id and last_sequence, read, inserted and updated by any connection holding a grant, never deleted); on a database our repository built it changes nothing. V0114 (r9: CR-182, CR-184, CR-191, CR-196) makes platform.idempotency_record unique on (operation_id, idempotency_key) with status completed only (a NOT VALID check: rows already there are not rechecked), re-applies the row-level security of orders.cart, orders.sales_order, orders.order_line and orders.order_event so a guest reads its own cart and orders (staff still by venue or scope) and of the 21 tables under them, and grants commerce SELECT on access.entitlement and access.scan_event where the commerce role exists. V0115 (r9: CR-146) puts five foreign keys in the reference's form: rental.booking's deposit key now points at orders.payment, platform.configuration_profile's primary key is widened (its old key and the keys onto it replaced first) and platform.profile_deployment's key onto it is on (profile_id, version), venuemap.visit_plan's subject key points at pii.subject, and platform.workstation gains its key onto configuration_profile, each added NOT VALID and doing nothing where the key is already the reference's. How to check (in psql, each answers true): `select to_regclass('catalogue.inventory_reservation') is not null and to_regclass('catalogue.inventory_hold') is null;` `select to_regclass('wallet.fund_reservation') is not null and to_regclass('wallet.hold') is null;` `select to_regclass('seating.seat_reservation') is not null and to_regclass('seating.seat_hold') is null;` `select to_regclass('sync.guest_link') is not null and to_regclass('platform.guest_link') is null;` (a check whose new and old names are both null is a table your database never had: that is fine), and `select version from platform.schema_version where version like 'V01%' order by version;` lists the number of every tenant file above in the tenant database, and of every control file above in control (an older V0100 to V0102 may be there too). Done when: applied and checked, or, if your local database has none of the tables these files touch, close this task as not needed with a one-line comment saying so.

tasks.subject: identity.delegated_access: a guest's household grant passes the write check (CR-362)
tasks.detail: Spec: ADAM CR-362, the lead's decision of 30 October 2026 (posted on its ticket), in the contracts at the release tag in ADAM. The [DB] work of #30672 (grantDelegation), carried by this task. One forward migration in the tenant database. (1) A new function platform.subject_holds_household_grant_over(over_subject_id uuid) returns boolean: STABLE, plpgsql (so it is not inlined), not SECURITY DEFINER; true when an identity.delegated_access row exists with subject_id = current_setting('ticvai.subject_id'), over_subject_id = the argument, delegation_kind familyMember or primaryHolder, effect ALLOW, revoked_at null and now inside valid_from/valid_to. It reads only the guest's own held grants, which the read policy already shows the guest. tasks.subject: Marketing sends a guest's one-time code: sendGuestOneTimeCode and the guestOneTimeCode system template (CR-370)
tasks.detail: Spec: ADAM CR-370, the lead's decision of 30 October 2026, in the contracts at the release tag in ADAM (contracts/satellite/marketing-crm.yaml sendGuestOneTimeCode; the event identity.guestCodeIssued v1). Identity and Marketing are in different deployables, so the code reaches Marketing by an outbox event: requestGuestOtp, registerGuest (channel email) and verifyGuestEmail (mode send) write identity.guestCodeIssued in the transaction that writes the identity.otp_challenge row, with the destination and the code field-encrypted (KERNEL-FIELD-ENC). This task is Marketing's side. sendGuestOneTimeCode is invoked by the relay, as notifyPerformanceHolders is: it decrypts the destination and code at send time, sends on the event's channel through the tenant's configured provider with the system template guestOneTimeCode in the guest's language (the template carries its own subject), and writes a transactional marketing.message_dispatch row without the code. It is idempotent on challengeId; once expiresAt has passed it stops retrying and is not dead-lettered for replay. Seed the system template guestOneTimeCode (English and Arabic) with the other system templates. Until KERNEL-FIELD-ENC is Ready for QA, Identity keeps IGuestCodeDelivery's log-only default, and a code is never in clear in the outbox. Done when: an event for an email and an SMS challenge each sends one message in the guest's language and writes one dispatch row without the code; a second delivery of the same event sends nothing; an event past expiresAt is dropped without a dead letter; no log line or stored row holds the code or the destination in clear.

tasks.subject: platform.tenant_field_key and platform.blind_index_rehash: where field-encryption keys and re-hash progress are kept (CR-339)
tasks.detail: Spec: ADAM CR-339, the lead's decision of 30 October 2026 (posted on its ticket), in the contracts at the release tag in ADAM. The [DB] work of #27665 (MIG-PLATFORM): that ticket has started, so its text is not rewritten, and this task carries the database part of the decision. One forward migration, additive, in every tenant database: two new tables only the kernel reads and writes (KERNEL-FIELD-ENC). (1) platform.tenant_field_key: id uuid primary key, purpose text CHECK in (dataKey, blindIndexKey), key_version integer NOT NULL, wrapped_key bytea NOT NULL, wrapping_key_id text NOT NULL (the Key Vault key and its version), state text CHECK in (active, decryptOnly, retired), created_at timestamptz NOT NULL, rotated_at timestamptz; the unique indexes tenant_field_key_purpose_key_version_uniq on (purpose, key_version) and tenant_field_key_purpose_uniq on (purpose) WHERE state = 'active' (V0120 lines 110 and 114); code that recognises a clash by constraint name uses these names (ADAM CR-461, 2 November 2026). tasks.subject: Catalogue's channel deployment job: a live dynamic price moves from executing to deployed, partly deployed or failed (CR-422)
tasks.detail: Spec: ADAM CR-422, the lead's decision of 31 October 2026 (posted on #35182, createLiveDynamicPrice), in the contracts at the release tag in ADAM (contracts/spine/catalogue.yaml createLiveDynamicPrice; the event catalogue.priceExecuted, events/catalogue-priceExecuted.yaml; states/price-execution.yaml). createLiveDynamicPrice (SVC-CATALOGUE-DRAFTED-25) writes one catalogue.price_execution and publishes catalogue.priceExecuted (executionId, strategyId, target, newPrice, channels) through the outbox; nothing then moves the execution, so this task is the consumer the event names: the channel deployment job in the workers host (ADR-0055), Catalogue's back end. For each event it deploys the new price to each channel named, and moves the execution as states/price-execution.yaml says: executing to deployed when every channel reports a consistent price, to partiallyDeployed when some did not, to failed when none accepted it (the previous price stays live), and partiallyDeployed to deployed when the failed channels are retried and succeed; each move writes the row and its catalogue.audit_entry in one transaction. tasks.subject: Marketing's message sender: the dispatch worker and the email, SMS and push providers (CR-442)
tasks.detail:
broadcastToGuests is built to CR-379: it records the broadcast, enqueues workforce.guestBroadcastAccepted and answers 202. Marketing's consumer, sendGuestBroadcast, works out every subject and channel, but cannot write what CR-379 asks. marketing.message_dispatch has no column for the broadcast it belongs to or for the text to send, and being partitioned by queued_at it cannot carry a unique key on broadcastId + subjectId + channel. Nothing in the repository sends push, SMS or email either: no dispatch worker, no provider adapter, and sendTransactionalMessage is not built. So today an evacuation is accepted with 202 and reaches no guest. The consumer dead-letters every delivery rather than pretend it sent anything, and #37101 cannot go to QA until this is settled.

**What was seen**

CR-379 (decided 31 Oct): "writes one transactional message_dispatch per subject and channel with sourceRef = broadcastId. It is idempotent on broadcastId + subjectId + channel." and "Drop the x-ticvai-write-via to sendTransactionalMessage."
CR-379's own problem text: "message_dispatch has no column for the body, kind or broadcast id" (not addressed by the decision).
db/tenant/038-marketing.sql, marketing.message_dispatch: columns id, subject_id, campaign_id, channel, template_id, message_trigger_id, campaign_variant_id, planned_send_at, status, failure_reason, provider_reference, queued_at, delivered_at, is_test, opened_at, clicked_at, complained_at, unsubscribed_at; "CONSTRAINT message_dispatch_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id, queued_at)) PARTITION BY RANGE (queued_at)". No source_ref, no body. CR-138 kept the partitioning.
A unique index on a partitioned table must include the partition key, so (broadcast, subject, channel) cannot be unique without queued_at.
src/: no push, SMS or email sender or dispatch worker exists; marketing-crm#sendTransactionalMessage is not built.

**Options considered**

- A: add source_ref uuid and body text (the resolved message) to marketing.message_dispatch, with a non-unique index on (source_ref, subject_id, channel). Idempotency comes from the consumer's inbox: every dispatch of one delivery is written in the inbox's transaction, plus a check before insert. A separate ticket builds the dispatch worker and the push, SMS and email providers.
- B: a Marketing-owned table guest_broadcast_dispatch (broadcast_id, subject_id, channel, body, status, provider_reference, queued_at, sent_at) with a unique key on (broadcast_id, subject_id, channel); the dispatch worker and providers as in A.
- C: un-partition marketing.message_dispatch so the unique key can exist (reverses CR-138).

**Recommended**

A. It keeps every guest message in one table, as CR-379 intends, and stays within ADR-0056's partitioning. The inbox already de-duplicates deliveries at least once. Whichever option is chosen, the dispatch worker and the three channel providers need their own ticket: until they exist, a 202 evacuation reaches nobody. Until then broadcastToGuests stays as built and #37101 stays On hold.

**Intake**

- Source: developer — #37101
- Triage: defect, now
- Contract impact: none
- Artefacts: tenancy#broadcastToGuests, marketing-crm#sendTransactionalMessage, workforce.guest_broadcast
- Raised against release r11

**Decision (CR-442 · accepted)**

Decided (Chinmay, 1 November 2026): A. marketing.message_dispatch keeps source_ref (r12 already adds it: the [DB] ticket for CR-379) and gains body text, nullable: the resolved message as sent. Add a non-unique index on (source_ref, subject_id, channel). Idempotency comes from the consumer's inbox: every dispatch row of one delivery is written in the inbox's transaction, after a check that no row for that source_ref, subject_id and channel exists. The partitioning stays (ADR-0056). The sending itself is a new ticket, filed as a child of this one: Marketing's message sender, the dispatch worker that sends queued dispatch rows through the provider each channel has configured (setChannelProvider: email, SMS and push, ranked by role and priority with fallback) and records delivered or failed with the provider's reference. Guest one-time codes (CR-370) send through the same worker. Until it exists broadcastToGuests stays as built, the consumer dead-letters rather than pretending to send, and #37101 stays On hold. Build to it now; the package is updated to match at the next release.

---

Raised in ADAM as CR-442 (Backend).

**Done when (plan):** a queued marketing.message_dispatch row is sent through the provider its channel has configured (setChannelProvider: by role and priority, falling back on failure) and marked delivered or failed with the provider's reference; a guest one-time code (CR-370) goes through the same worker; a channel with no provider fails the row and never reports it delivered.

tasks.subject: Device-key sign-in for apiKeyAuth operations (signage displays, queue readings) (CR-451)
tasks.detail:
getSignageQueueBoard and getSignageQueueCalls are device calls from a signage display: security apiKeyAuth, no permission, audience device, scope level venue. Nothing in the package or the repository defines a display key: tenancy.device_credential.kind allows only clientCertificate, deviceToken and mutualTls; platform.device has no key column; the request kernel has no device session and nothing reads X-Api-Key. So neither endpoint can sign a display in, check that the venueId or queueId it asks for is its own, or answer 401. The read behind getSignageQueueCalls is built (unexposed); both endpoints wait on this. submitQueueReading has the same gap.

**What was seen**

queue.yaml (around L1376, L1413): "security: - apiKeyAuth: []", "x-ticvai-permission: null # a registered device, authenticated by its enrolment rather than a person", "x-ticvai-audience: [device]", "x-ticvai-scope-level: venue". The board's description: "Unauthenticated by display key". Scheme: "apiKeyAuth: {type: apiKey, in: header, name: X-Api-Key}".
tenancy.device_credential.kind check: clientCertificate, deviceToken, mutualTls.
submitQueueReading (around L1258) uses the same scheme.

**Options considered**

- A: define a display key: a device_credential of kind apiKey holding only a hash, bound to a signageDisplay device and its venue. The key opens a session scoped to that venue; venueId and queueId must be inside it; a missing or wrong key is 401. A ticket builds the device-key sign-in for every apiKeyAuth operation.
- B: use the existing deviceToken credential as a bearer token, and change these operations' security from apiKeyAuth to it.
- C: make the signage reads public by venueId (guest or public audience, like getWaitTimes), with no key.

**Recommended**

A: a display holds no person's session, the key can be revoked per device, and venue scope stays enforced. It needs a ticket for the device-key sign-in, which submitQueueReading also needs.

**Intake**

- Source: developer — #33061
- Triage: scope, now
- Contract impact: additive
- Artefacts: queue#getSignageQueueCalls, queue#submitQueueReading, tenancy.device_credential, platform.device
- Raised against release r11

**Decision (CR-451 · accepted)**

Decided (Chinmay, 1 November 2026): as you recommended (A). A display key is a tenancy.device_credential of a new kind apiKey, holding only a hash of the key, bound to one signage display device and its venue; the key is shown once when issued and can be revoked per device. A request with X-Api-Key opens a device session scoped to that venue; a venueId or queueId outside it is 403, a missing, wrong or revoked key is 401. The sign-in is a new ticket, filed as a child of this one: device-key sign-in for every apiKeyAuth operation (issue, hash and store, verify, revoke; the kind check gains apiKey), which getSignageQueueBoard, getSignageQueueCalls and submitQueueReading all use. #33061 stays On hold until it is built. Build to it now; the package is updated to match at the next release.

---

Raised in ADAM as CR-451 (Backend).

**Done when (plan):** a signage display with a valid key (a tenancy.device_credential of kind apiKey, stored only as a hash, shown once when issued) reads its venue's board and calls; a venueId or queueId outside its venue is 403; a missing, wrong or revoked key is 401; submitQueueReading signs in the same way; and Tenancy's in-process query tenancy#deviceForApiKey (contracts/spine/tenancy.yaml x-ticvai-queries; the lead, 2 November 2026: "yes for both"), built with this ticket, answers the device, its kind and its venue for a live key's hash and nothing for any other, in one statement under the routed tenant's root grant, asked in process from commerce and the operations host with the operations role's read grant of XDR-068 (R13-DB-IN-PROCESS-READ-GRANTS, which this task follows).

tasks.subject: Catalogue's channel retry job: carry out a queued incident retry and move the incident on (CR-457)
tasks.detail:
**[CR-457] [BE] Catalogue's channel retry job: carry out a queued incident retry and move the incident on**

From ADAM CR-457 (#35231), decided by Chinmay on 2 November 2026. The work: [BE] Catalogue's channel retry job: carry out a queued incident retry (catalogue.channelIncidentRetryRequested) and move the incident to resolved or investigating

**The decision (also the ADAM CR-457 comment on #35231):**

Decided (Chinmay, 2 November 2026): A, as you recommended: the retry is a fact written to the outbox and carried out by a job. Build now: (1) retryChannelIncident, in one transaction: an incident that is resolved or closed answers 409 not-retryable and nothing changes. Otherwise move the catalogue.channel_incident to retrying, add 1 to retry_count and set updated_at. If api_request_reference is null, set it to the incident id as text, so this retry and every later one share one reference. Write one catalogue.audit_entry (domain channel, action retry, entity_type channelIncident, entity_id the incident). Write one platform.outbox row for catalogue.channelIncidentRetryRequested v1 (aggregate channelIncident, aggregateId the incident id). Answer 202 with the incident, and declare x-ticvai-emits catalogue.channelIncidentRetryRequested on the operation. (2) The event, for events/catalogue-channelIncidentRetryRequested.yaml when the package catches up: publisher catalogue; emittedWhen 'retryChannelIncident moves an incident from open or investigating to retrying'; emittedBy retryChannelIncident. Payload: incidentId (uuid), salesChannelId (uuid), channelConnectionId (uuid, optional), errorType (string), apiRequestReference (string, the partner's idempotency reference, reused unchanged), correlationId (string, optional, the original call's trace id, used only to find the trace and never sent to the partner as the idempotency reference), retryCount (integer), requestedByPrincipalId (uuid). Consumer: Catalogue's channel retry job in the workers host; idempotency key incidentId + retryCount; onFailure retryThenDeadLetter; isCritical false. Retention 30 days after publication. (3) The job (its own ticket): if the incident is no longer retrying, or its retry_count is not the event's, do nothing. Otherwise find the failed call's trace in catalogue.audit_entry (domain channel, reference equal to the incident's original apiRequestReference, or by correlationId when it had none), and send that call again through the channel connector for channelConnectionId, with apiRequestReference as the partner's idempotency reference. Product, price and availability calls send today's values, not the stale ones; order and cancellation calls send the same request. On the partner's success, set status resolved, resolved_at now and resolution_note 'Retry <retry_count> succeeded'. On failure, set status investigating, and take error_code and response_excerpt from the answer (truncated and scrubbed of personal data). Until a connector exists for the connection's type, the attempt fails with error_code connectorNotAvailable; an incident is never marked resolved without a partner's success. If the event is dead-lettered, move the incident to investigating with error_code retryNotDelivered, so nothing stays retrying. Each move writes the incident and one catalogue.audit_entry (domain channel, result success or failure, source sync, actor_system channelRetryJob) in one transaction. Build to it now; the package is updated to match at the next release.

No release carries it: build to this text now; the package catches up later.

**Done when (plan):** a catalogue.channelIncidentRetryRequested event moves the incident to resolved only on the partner's success, otherwise to investigating with error_code and response_excerpt (connectorNotAvailable until a connector exists); an event whose incident is no longer retrying or whose retry_count moved on does nothing; a dead-lettered event leaves the incident investigating with retryNotDelivered; every move writes its catalogue.audit_entry in the same transaction.

tasks.subject: Kiosk prints through the Windows device host: status, print job, printer errors on KSK-010 (CR-463)
tasks.detail:
**[CR-463] [FE] Kiosk prints through the Windows device host: status, print job, printer errors on KSK-010**

From ADAM CR-463 (#35592), decided by Chinmay on 2 November 2026. The work: [FE] Kiosk and POS print through the Windows device host: status check, print job with the filled layout, and the printer errors routed to KSK-010 and POS-026 (one child per app: kiosk and POS)

**The decision (also the ADAM CR-463 comment on #35592):**

Decided (Chinmay, 2 November 2026): A, as you recommended: the device host's API as built is the contract, written down once, and the Android path implements the same one later. Build now: (1) The host's OpenAPI 3 file, as built on feature/35592-boca-windows-device-host, is the spec. It covers GET /ticket-printer/status and POST /ticket-printer/print-jobs (Idempotency-Key required), with errors as application/problem+json in the shared Problem shape and the problem types as built: paper out, jam, offline, busy and fault are 503; printer-rejected-ticket is 502; print-not-confirmed is 504; stock-not-configured and the two RFID codes are 409; validation is 400. The TicketLayout names are as built (stock with widthMm, heightMm and dpi; elements with kind, xMm, yMm, rotation, font, fontSize and moduleSizeMm; content as field, text or assetRef). Commit the file to the host's repository and attach it to #35592. The package adds it as contracts/devices/ticket-printer.yaml, with TicketLayout in the orders contract, under the same names, so the host does not change. (2) Part of the contract: the host listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It answers only the kiosk and POS app origins named in its local settings (CORS and the private-network preflight) and refuses any other origin with 403. tasks.subject: catalogue.variant gains price_category_id, nullable, with its index (CR-455)
tasks.detail:
**[CR-455] [DB] catalogue.variant gains price_category_id, nullable, with its index**

From ADAM CR-455 (#35288), decided by Chinmay on 2 November 2026. The work: [DB] catalogue.variant gains price_category_id, nullable, with its index (CR-455)

**The decision (also the ADAM CR-455 comment on #35288):**

Decided (Chinmay, 2 November 2026): A1, A2 and A3, with corrections. Build now: (1) Price category: add catalogue.variant.price_category_id uuid NULL, with index variant_price_category_id_idx and a conventional reference to catalogue.price_category, in a forward migration. ProductVariant gains an optional nullable priceCategoryId. updateProductVariant writes it and listProductVariants answers it; no screen changes. In variantPriceRecords (CR-439), once the winning candidate is chosen, the category amount applies when the variant has a price_category_id and the winning assignment's category_rates has an entry whose rateId names a catalogue.rate that is in the winning price list, has status active and has price_category_id equal to the variant's. That rate's amount then replaces price.amount. A rate with a null amount takes its base_rate_id rate's amount adjusted by adjustment_type and adjustment_value: percentage multiplies by (1 + value/100), fixedAmount adds value. The entry's priceCategory string is not matched; the rate's own price_category_id is. A variant with no category, or with no matching entry, keeps price.amount. (2) When no price resolves, simulatePriceBreakdownCalculation answers 422 no-selected-rate, as the contract states. CR-439's no-price-for-variant is not used, and searchCatalogue and getVariantListing answer a null price. (3) Member adjustment, at the contextualRateSelection step. A candidate is a pricing.dynamic_price_rule row with is_active true and valid_from <= at < valid_to (a null bound is open), where at is the instant variantPriceRecords is asked at. Its product_id is null or productId; its price_list_id is null or the winning list; its channel_id is null or the venue's catalogue.sales_channel id for the channel; its sales_channel is null or the channel. It also has a membershipProgramme condition (CR-439) whose value_json lists membershipId. With condition_logic all, every other condition must hold, and a condition the simulation has no input for does not hold. The lowest priority number wins, then the latest valid_from, then id, and only one rule applies. Its pricing.dynamic_price_action works by type: percentAdjustment multiplies the rate by (1 + value/100); fixedAmountAdjustment adds value; returnToBase leaves the selected rate unchanged. moveToBand is not applied, because the action keeps no band; the component's reason says so. The result is clamped to the action's min_price and max_price where they are set. With no membershipId, or no matching rule, there is no memberAdjustment component. (4) Dynamic adjustment. The step is skipped when the winning candidate came through a catalogue.price_assignment with is_dynamic_pricing_allowed false. Otherwise take the catalogue.price_execution with status deployed or partiallyDeployed, product_id = productId, event_id null or eventId, and performance_id null or timeslotId (a timeslotId is a catalogue.performance id; there is no timeslot table). It must also have a channel_deployments entry for the simulated channel, mapped as in CR-422 (web is b2c, mobile is mobileApp, callCentre is callCenter, the rest by the same name). Prefer the most specific (performance, then event, then product only), then the newest created_at, then id. Its price is that channel entry's price, else new_price. (5) Fees. A candidate is a catalogue.fee_rule with rule_kind applicability, status active and in effect at at, set at the venue's scope or above, whose catalogue.fee is active and in effect. Every condition key it sets must match: productId; productCategoryId (the product's category_id); salesChannel; venueId; eventId; membership (membershipId); paymentMethod; deliveryMethod; marketCode (the product's market_code); quantityMin and quantityMax (quantity); orderValueMin and orderValueMax (the subtotal after the price steps). customerType, transactionType, countryCode, serviceAction, hoursBeforeEventMax and deliveryDestinationZones have no simulation input, so a rule that sets one does not match. Evaluate in priority order, lower number first, then id. A matching rule is skipped when a rule of its mutual_exclusion_group has already applied, or when its fee was excluded by a rule that applied. combination stack (or null) adds the fee. replace removes the applied fees named in excluded_fee_ids, then adds this one. exclude adds this one and keeps the named fees out for the rest of the run. on_match stopProcessing ends the run. The amount: fixedAmount is amount; percentage is that percentage of the subtotal; tiered takes the tiers entry with the largest fromOrderValue at or below the subtotal, and charges its amount or its percentage of the subtotal. The fee is charged once when application is applyOnce or charge_basis is perOrder, perTransaction or perDay; otherwise it is charged per item, times quantity. The component type is surcharge for fee_type surcharge and fee for every other type. An exception rule applies only when all of these hold: eligibility_basis is membershipBenefit; eligibility_ref_id is null or membershipId; a membershipId is sent; and is_approval_required and is_evidence_required are both false. Then feeWaiver zeroes the fees in target_fee_ids, feeReduction takes reduction_percent or reduction_amount off them, and taxExemption and zeroRatedTax zero the taxes of target_tax_profile_ids, each shown as a waiver component. No other exception rule is applied. (6) Taxes. A candidate is a catalogue.tax_rule with status active and in effect at at, at the venue's scope or above. Each condition it sets must equal the simulation's value: product_id, product_category_id, venue_id, legal_entity_id (the winning price list's) and sales_channel. A rule that sets country_code, transaction_type or customer_type does not match. The most specific wins: the most conditions set, then product before category before venue, then the latest effective_from, then id. Its treatment applies, so the rule wins over ledger.tax_code.is_inclusive. With no matching rule, the winning price's catalogue.price.tax_code_id applies, inclusive when that code's is_inclusive is true. With none at all, no tax is charged, and a zero tax component says so. The rule's taxes entries apply in their sequence. For each entry, read its catalogue.tax_profile, then the rate of the profile's tax_code_id through finance#taxCodeRecords, and apply that rate to the profile's tax_base. onPreviousTaxes adds the earlier taxes to the base. taxInclusive takes the tax out of the amount; taxExclusive adds it on top; taxExempt, zeroRated and outOfScope give a zero tax component carrying that treatment. A fee is taxed by the tax rule its tax_treatment names, and a fee with an empty tax_treatment is not taxed. Build the percentage, compound, sequential and multipleConcurrent methods now. fixedTax and tiered answer 422 unsupported-tax-method, which is added to the operation's 422 problem types; both methods go on the left-out list. (7) finance#taxCodeRecords: build it yourself in #35288, inside the Ledger module behind its query interface: one read of ledger.tax_code by ids under the caller's row security. No other ticket builds it, and #31818 calls it. (8) Put the price, fee and tax steps in one Catalogue calculation component rather than inside the endpoint, so that checkout can call the same code later. The promotion rule of CR-439 stays as it is. Build to it now; the package is updated to match at the next release.

No release carries it: build to this text now; the package catches up later.

**Done when (plan):** catalogue.variant has price_category_id, nullable, with variant_price_category_id_idx and its reference to catalogue.price_category; a second run of the migration changes nothing.

tasks.subject: Platform sign-in: the Control Plane signs a platform operator in and issues the platform token, and every cell host verifies it and builds the platform caller (ADR-0072)
tasks.detail: The platform-auth ticket ADR-0072 section 6 asks for (ADAM CR-175, option A, accepted 21 October 2026; CHG-R10ID-007), scheduled before listOwnPlatformStaffGrants (#30739) and openPlatformStaffGrant (#30742). (1) The Control Plane issues the platform token: a signed JWT, issuer https://<control-plane-host>/, signed with a Control Plane key held in Key Vault (ADR-0063); its public keys are published as a JWKS that every cell host trusts, configured per environment and never fetched from a URL the token names; audience the cell the call goes to (control.cell.id), so a token for one cell opens nothing in another; lifetime at most 15 minutes, refreshed by the Platform Console from its platform session. Key rotation: publish the new key before signing with it and keep the old one until the longest token has expired. (2) Claims: sub is the operator (control.platform_operator.id, a Control Plane principal, never a tenant identity.principal); ticvai_platform_permissions is the operator's PLATFORM_* set and nothing else; sid is the platform session (control.platform_session.id); amr includes mfa once the operator has passed the second factor in that session; ticvai_step_up is {action, at}, the last MFA step-up. (3) The Control Plane sign-in writes control.platform_operator (the operator and its PLATFORM_* set), control.platform_session (one sign-in to the Console, with its step-up) and control.platform_operator_mfa (its second factors; a totp secret and an emailOtp destination stored encrypted under the Control Plane's field key, since the control database has no tenant key); the three tables are the control database's (backend/control/V0116). An operator never has a credential, a principal or a session in a tenant database (R098). (4) The step-up is recorded on the platform session (step_up_action, step_up_at) and carried in ticvai_step_up; a cell operation that declares x-ticvai-step-up: mfa for a platform caller accepts it when ticvai_step_up.action names the operation, ticvai_step_up.at is within 5 minutes and amr includes mfa, and never looks for an identity.mfa_challenge row. (5) In every cell host (commerce, access, operations, workers; ADR-0055) the verification of the token and the platform caller built from it: the operator id, the PLATFORM_* set and the step-up, with no tenant scope until a platform-staff grant is open; a PLATFORM_* permission is honoured only on the operations that name it (R203); while a grant is open the operator's tenant permissions are the grant's, at the tenant root, and every action is audited with the grant's id. Until this lands, #30739 and #30742 are built against the platform caller with a test double; they follow this task only for the connection to the real token. The Control Plane's own operations (licensing, subscription, createTenant) and replayEvents do not wait on it: they check PLATFORM_* or DEVELOPER_MANAGE through the Control Plane's current principal. Done when: an operator signs in with its second factor and gets a token for one cell that a host of that cell accepts and a host of another cell refuses; a token past 15 minutes, signed by an unknown key or with the wrong audience is refused 401; openPlatformStaffGrant accepts a step-up of under 5 minutes for itself and refuses an older one or one for another action; a PLATFORM_* permission opens nothing on an operation that does not name it.

tasks.subject: CrossRegion: POST /sync-rejections and the resolution route over serviceAuth, with their 401s (CR-241)
tasks.detail: Spec: ADAM CR-241, option B (the lead, 26 October 2026; CHG-R10CRF-001, CHG-R10CRF-013), in the contracts at the release tag in ADAM (contracts/spine/cross-region.yaml recordSyncRejection and recordSyncRejectionResolution). tasks.subject: whitelabel.config_version keeps when a version became current (activated_at), and each tenant's current version takes its published_at (CR-154)
tasks.detail: Spec: ADAM CR-154 and R8 blocker IDENTITY-C63, the lead's scheduled-publish decision posted to Narayan Gaonkar on 2 November 2026 for #27779 (publishTenantConfig and the scheduled-publish job, white-label#scheduledPublish), in the contracts at the release tag in ADAM (white-label.yaml ConfigVersion.activatedAt): "whitelabel.config_version gains activated_at timestamptz NULL (ConfigVersion.activatedAt), set whenever a version becomes current (an immediate publishTenantConfig or the job); backfill each tenant's current version with its published_at." The [DB] work of that decision on whitelabel.config_version, created by MIG-WHITELABEL (#27663; its sub-task #30254, [DB] whitelabel.config_version; both started, not rewritten): a developer does not write a migration, so this task carries it. One guarded forward migration in the tenant database: (1) ALTER TABLE whitelabel.config_version ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS activated_at timestamptz, nullable: when the version became current, set by an immediate publishTenantConfig, the approval consumer or the scheduled-publish job; (2) UPDATE whitelabel.config_version SET activated_at = published_at WHERE is_current: each tenant's current version takes its published_at, and every other version keeps null, which the job reads as never made current. No NOT NULL: a version not yet current has none. Source DDL after r1: the statements on whitelabel.config_version in the forward migration the release derives for it (backend/tenant/V01nn__after_r1_<date>.sql, at the release tag in ADAM); write the migration yourself, copied from those statements, each guarded so it applies twice. It reaches the server databases as that release file, applied when the lead says (they are frozen until then); the developers build and test against it locally first. Test: after the migration each tenant's current version has activated_at equal to its published_at and every other version has null. Done when: applied to a database at the previous state it makes exactly these changes, a second run changes nothing, and the result matches the package's derived DDL at the release tag.

Used by setChannelConnectionConfiguration (#35232: credentialsReference and certificateReference when not null, 422 secret-not-reference) and by KERNEL-SECRET-STORE, which names the secrets it writes in the same form and follows this task. Done when: a reference with the caller's tenant prefix passes; another tenant's prefix, a pasted key, upper case, a name over 119 characters or ending in a dash are refused; the refused value appears in no problem, log or audit entry; and a peer in the same stack has reviewed and tested it.

tasks.subject: One-off job after the r14 migration: rental.participant.id_number encrypted into pii.subject_document, and the 18 moved contact fields copied into pii.subject_contact through Identity, each count verified (CHG-R14M-001)
tasks.detail: Spec: CHG-R14M-001 (the lead, 3 November 2026: "Move the columns"), ADR-0063 (field encryption) and the "personal data moved" rows of handoff/migration-review.md, in the contracts at the release tag in ADAM. Two kinds of moved value cannot be copied in SQL, so this job carries them, after the r14 tenant migration has run: (1) a participant's ID number, which pii.subject_document holds encrypted with the tenant's field key (the database never holds it): each rental.participant row with an id_number is encrypted through IFieldEncryption into pii.subject_document for the row's pii.subject; (2) the 18 moved contact fields (email, phone, mobile and contact point: identity.principal.email, workforce.employee email and mobile, marketing.guest_profile email and phone, and the rest marked contact.* in those rows), which pii.subject_contact holds with Identity's deterministic value hash: each is written through Identity (recordSubjectDetails) for the row's subject. The r14 migration only counts these rows; the job verifies its own counts against them and stops on any mismatch. It is idempotent on the source row and writes nothing twice. The old columns are not cleared or retired in r14 (that waits for the lead). Done when: every source row has its pii.subject_document or pii.subject_contact whose value equals the old one, a second run writes nothing, and the job's counts equal the migration's counts.

readViaBuiltWithNote: query (`<module>#<name>`, an x-ticvai-queries entry an operation's x-ticvai-read-via asks) -> the operations its module answers it from; tools/build-service-docs.py makes the asking operation's task wait on their tasks (CHG-TKT-014, ADAM CR-085: closeFiscalPeriod waits on Wallet's period-close query, built in Block A by the lead's decision 6 of 14 October 2026). A query with no entry adds no wait. An entry may name the operation whose ticket builds a query class of another module, and tools/op-descriptions.py names the query on that operation's ticket: 2 November 2026 (CHG-R13PL-051; ADAM CR-447, the lead: "yes for both"), Access's access#mediaTemplateRecords is built with orders printTicketProof (#31680), which asks it in process.
operationWaitsNote: operation -> the hand-written plan tasks its task waits for: an operation whose ticket needs work that no screen, operation or query of the plan implies (a kernel scheme or client it runs on). tools/build-service-docs.py makes the task that builds the operation wait on each task named, so the release links the two tasks; a key must be a task of this file (a generated key, such as a migration's, is only settled at the key reconcile, and the build stops on one). Added 29 October 2026 (CHG-R11PLN-001; ADAM CR-271, CR-281 to CR-284): the lead made the four kernel tickets that day and linked each of these operations' tickets to the kernel tickets it waits for by hand in OpenProject; this is the plan's record of those waits. 31 October 2026 (CHG-R12PL-012; ADAM CR-343): setAnalyticsProvider and setMaintenanceMode no longer wait on KERNEL-SERVICE-AUTH: the only read they needed the service route for, tenancy#activeVenues, is asked in process from the operations host. 31 October 2026 (CHG-R12PL-033; ADAM CR-418): listLearningModelPerformance (#35225) waits on AI-ENGINE-PRICE-OUTCOME-MEASURE, the AI engineers' specification of how an executed price's actual outcome is measured, which its scorecards are assembled from (the lead, 31 October 2026: "the AI engineers specify the price outcome measure now; ADM-117 stays in Block A"). 2 November 2026 (CHG-R13PL-018; ADAM CR-175, ADR-0072 section 6): listOwnPlatformStaffGrants (#30739) and openPlatformStaffGrant (#30742) wait on PLATFORM-AUTH, for the connection to the real platform token only; they are built against the platform caller with a test double meanwhile, and the Control Plane's own operations and replayEvents do not wait on it. 2 November 2026 (CHG-R13PL-019 to CHG-R13PL-027; the lead: "Can you check for all the missing tickets as well"): setApprovalExternalProvider, changeOwnCredential and forceLogout wait on KERNEL-SECRET-STORE (CR-243); createApprovalRequest on CR330-PLATFORM-APPROVAL-RULE-DB (CR-330); broadcastToGuests and sendGuestBroadcast on CR379-LIVE-ENTITLEMENT-SUBJECTS (CR-379); setSsoConfig and completeSsoAuthorization on CR327-DB-SSO-PROVIDER-AUDIENCE (CR-327). appModulesNote: A decided app-module (Chinmay, 5 October 2026, CHG-R4-003; docs/active/decisions/answers-5-october.md): work the lead places in a named block as one app-module, which no screen-module rule would form. tools/build-service-docs.py builds it as written: `operations` are built by its back-end tasks (grouped by service and tag as usual) and the tables they need by its forward migration; `screens` are built whole by its front-end tasks under their usual keys; each `wiring` entry is one front-end task (`key`) that wires `operations` into `screens` another ticket builds, so that ticket's scope, points and waits stay as they were and its text names the wiring task; `tasks` names hand-written tasks of this file (with `block` and `appModule`) built in it; `scheduleAfter` (a block) puts its tasks behind that block's in the build order, so a module added after the block's tickets were pushed moves none of their owners or sprints and takes the capacity left. `block` is kept: the block-filling and pass-2 moves never move a decided app-module. tools/check-plan-closure.py reads the wiring (an operation a screen binds through a wiring task is wired in that task's drop).

appModules.name: White Label · Kiosk customisation
appModules.decided: Chinmay, 5 October 2026 (docs/active/decisions/answers-5-october.md): Block "A2"; "we add it as release now to make sure that it goes out"; "it is a addition so it shouldnt break existing" (CHG-R4-001, CHG-R4-003)
appModules.why: The kiosk becomes the third channel of the white-label builder: a kiosk configuration per kiosk group (device profile, attract loop, start tiles, header and footer, journey, session, payment and output, languages, messages, hours), published per group with versions and roll back, assigned to kiosks on ADM-582 and read by the kiosk shell. Block A2 (ends Friday 11 December 2026, Sprint 5), not A1: no A1 ticket's scope, points or waits change.

wiring.subject: Kiosk shell: the published kiosk configuration on KSK-001, KSK-002, KSK-008, KSK-010, KSK-013 and KSK-014
wiring.detail: The kiosk shell reads its group's published kiosk configuration (getPublishedKioskConfig, keyed by the kiosk's workstation) at start and at every return to the attract loop, caches it with the loop's media for offline, and applies it: KSK-001 plays the attract loop (the group's slides, transition, sound, play windows, the closed loop outside the opening hours, the Download our app QR slide) under Touch to start, and runs the idle rule on every kiosk screen (Still there? with its countdown, then the cart cleared, the guest signed out, back to the loop in the default language); KSK-002 offers the group's languages with its default; KSK-008, KSK-010 and KSK-013 show the group's payment unresolved, printer failure and call staff messages; KSK-014 shows the group's out of service message and expected-back time. Offline the last cached loop plays and nothing is sold.

wiring.subject: ADM-582 POS, Kiosk & Terminal Assignment Manager: put a kiosk in a kiosk group
wiring.detail: ADM-582 gains the kiosks and their groups: the list of the venue's kiosks with the kiosk group each is in (listKioskAssignments), the venue's kiosk groups to choose from (listKioskConfigs, the default first) and Put in kiosk group (assignKiosk; null puts the kiosk back on the venue's default, 409 when the workstation is not a kiosk).
